| "4개 절로" | 절 수를 지정합니다. 3~12절 범위입니다. |
| "검토 보고서", "주간 보고", "회의록", "장애 보고" | 문서 종류에 맞는 구성을 적용합니다. 판단을 요구하는 문서에만 요약과 권고 절이 포함됩니다. |
| **+** → 템플릿 고르기에서 템플릿 선택 | 해당 템플릿의 구성 규칙과 조판을 적용합니다. |

title: 보고서 작성
heading: 내보내기
text: 리본의 **파일 → 내보내기**에서 PDF, Word(DOCX), 한글(HWPX), 마크다운 원문, 인쇄를 선택합니다. 근거가 확인되지 않은 항목이 있으면 내보내기 전에 안내합니다. PDF는 테마를 그대로 반영하고, DOCX는 편집하기 좋은 구조를 우선합니다.

title: 요청으로 수정
text:
작성이 끝난 보고서와 슬라이드 하단의 입력창에 수정할 내용을 입력합니다. 요청 내용을 분석해 수정할 부분과 방식을 자동으로 판단합니다. 문장 단위 수정이나 장 순서 변경은 아티팩트 편집기를 사용하는 편이 빠릅니다.

| 요청 예시 | 처리 방식 |
|---|---|
| "2번 절을 절반으로 줄여 주세요", "결론에 일정 표를 추가해 주세요" | 해당 부분만 다시 작성합니다. 나머지는 유지됩니다. |
| "2절의 표는 빼고, 맨 앞에 3줄 요약을 넣어 주세요" | 요청마다 그 요청이 가리키는 절만 다시 작성합니다. 요약은 첫 절 맨 앞에 「핵심」 상자로 요청한 줄 수만큼 넣고, 제목·작성자 줄을 되풀이하지 않습니다. |
| "표 2와 그림 1은 빼 주세요" | 번호로 가리킨 표·그림을 다시 쓰지 않고 그대로 뺍니다. 그 표·그림을 가리키던 문장도 정리하고, 뒤의 표·그림 번호와 본문 속 번호를 당겨 맞춥니다. 같은 요청으로 그 절을 다시 쓸 때도 뺀 자리에 새 표·그림을 넣지 않습니다. 없는 번호는 찾지 못했다고 알려 드립니다. |
| "전체적으로 더 간결하게", "말투를 존댓말로" | 모든 부분을 다시 작성합니다. |
| "20장으로 늘려 주세요", "3장 추가", "2번과 3번을 합쳐 주세요", "순서를 바꿔 주세요" | 구성을 다시 제안하고 승인을 받은 뒤 작성합니다. 유지할 부분은 기존 제목을 그대로 사용합니다. |
| "지금 슬라이드가 몇 장이야?"처럼 문서에 대해 묻는 말 | 질문에는 이 화면에서 답하지 않고 바꾼 것도 없습니다. 고칠 곳을 알려 달라고 안내하고, 내용을 물으려면 내려받은 파일을 챗에 첨부해 물어보라고 알려 드립니다. |
| "새로 써 주세요", "처음부터 다시", "다른 주제로" | 기존 문서를 유지한 채 새로 작성합니다. |

수정이 완료되면 요청마다 한 일을 알려 드리고(예: "2절의 표 2를 뺐습니다. 맨 앞에 3줄 요약을 넣었습니다. 1절을 고쳤습니다.") 패널에 즉시 반영됩니다. 찾지 못했거나 반영되지 않은 요청은 고쳤다고 하지 않고 따로 알려 드립니다. 슬라이드에서 요청한 모양(예: "3장을 표로")이나 그림 빼기가 새 슬라이드에 나타나지 않으면 고쳤다고 하지 않고, 반영되지 않은 항목을 알려 드립니다. "그림 빼 줘"는 자동으로 그린 도식까지 빼고 몇 장에서 무엇을 뺐는지 알려 드리며, 뺄 그림이 없으면 바꾼 것이 없다고 알려 드립니다. 그림은 없고 차트만 있으면 차트가 있는 장을 알려 드리고 무엇을 뺄지 되묻습니다. "4장 차트 빼 줘"는 차트를 빼고, 빈 장에는 차트의 수치를 글머리표로 남깁니다. 수정할 때마다 이전 본문이 버전으로 저장됩니다.

부분 수정 시에도 최초 요청과 첨부 자료를 다시 참조합니다. 새로운 자료를 반영하려면 자료를 첨부한 상태에서 수정을 요청하십시오.

title: 공유
text: 대화 화면 오른쪽 위의 **공유** 버튼으로 링크를 생성합니다.

title: 공유
heading: 링크 생성
text:
1. 공개 범위를 선택합니다.

   | 범위 | 열람 가능한 대상 |
   |---|---|
   | 계정이 있는 사람 | 이 서비스에 로그인한 모든 사용자입니다. 부서나 팀 단위의 제한은 적용되지 않습니다. |
   | 링크가 있는 사람 | 링크를 아는 모든 사람이며 계정이 없어도 열람할 수 있습니다. |

2. **링크 만들기**를 누르고 **복사**합니다.

생성 후에는 상태가 **계정 필요** 또는 **계정 없이 열림**으로 표시됩니다.

title: 공유
heading: 공유되는 범위
text:
- 해당 대화와 그 대화에서 생성된 아티팩트가 공개됩니다. 아티팩트가 먼저 표시되고 대화가 이어집니다. 일부 종류는 공유 화면에서 아직 지원하지 않는다고 안내합니다.
- **프로젝트 파일과 메모리는 공유되지 않습니다.** 대화에 첨부한 파일은 답변에 인용된 범위까지 노출됩니다.
- **공유 이후에 이어지는 대화도 링크에 계속 반영됩니다.** 특정 시점까지만 공개하려면 링크를 철회하고 새로 생성하십시오.

title: 공유
heading: 열람 기록과 철회
text: 같은 창에서 열람자(이름과 이메일 또는 "계정 없는 방문자"), 브라우저, 지역, 열람 횟수를 확인할 수 있습니다. 한 시간 이내의 반복 열람은 한 번으로 집계합니다. **링크 철회**를 실행하면 해당 주소는 즉시 열리지 않습니다. 대화를 삭제한 경우에도 링크가 차단됩니다.

title: 슬라이드 작성
text: 홈에서 **슬라이드**를 선택하고 발표 주제와 대상을 입력합니다. 진행 절차는 보고서와 동일합니다. 확인 질문, **구성 확인**, **그림을 넣을까요?** 카드, 장 단위 작성 순으로 진행됩니다.

title: 슬라이드 작성
heading: 구성 확인 항목
text:
- 장 제목과 순서
- **어떻게 사용할 자료인가요?**: 발표하면서 설명 또는 자료만 전달

테마는 구성 카드에서 고르지 않습니다. 작성 후 패널에서 편집형, 미니멀, 포스터형, 분할형, 다크, 강철, 따뜻한, 파스텔, 숲, 학술, 흑백 중에서 선택합니다.

title: 슬라이드 작성
heading: 장 수 지정
text:
| 입력 예시 | 반영 내용 |
|---|---|
| "6장", "20장짜리" | 지정한 장 수로 작성합니다. 최대 50장입니다. |
| "20분 발표" | 2분당 1장을 기준으로 최소 장 수를 산출합니다. 20분이면 최소 10장입니다. |
| 지정하지 않음 | 주제에 맞춰 5~12장으로 작성합니다. |

6장을 초과하면 두 번째 장에 목차가 삽입됩니다.

title: 슬라이드 작성
heading: 장 유형
text: 모델이 내용에 맞는 유형을 선택합니다. 표지, 목차, 항목 나열, 표(비교), 지표(핵심 수치), 차트(자료에 수치가 있는 경우), 도식(흐름과 구조), 마무리를 사용합니다. "비교는 표로", "흐름도를 포함해"와 같이 요청문에 지정할 수 있습니다. 도식은 서버가 도형으로 그리며, PPTX로 내보내면 편집할 수 있는 PowerPoint 도형으로 들어갑니다. 제목이 구조·관계·흐름을 말하는 장("전체 구조", "핵심 오브젝트 관계도", "요청 처리 흐름")은 요청에 "구조도"라는 말이 없어도 도식을 넣고, 관계도는 순서 화살표가 아니라 관계 이름을 단 선으로 그립니다. 다 만든 뒤 "4장을 구조도로 바꿔 줘"라고 하면 그 장을 도식으로 바꿉니다. 영어로 쓴 덱은 도식의 글자와 설명도 영어입니다.

title: 슬라이드 작성
heading: 테마 변경
text: 패널의 **편집 › 테마** 탭에서 테마와 강조색을 변경하고 **이 장 다시 만들기**를 실행할 수 있습니다. 프로젝트에 테마가 연결되어 있으면 해당 색상과 서체를 따릅니다.

title: 슬라이드 작성
heading: 발표 모드
text: 리본의 **슬라이드 쇼**에서 전체 화면으로 전환합니다. `←` `→` 로 장을 이동하고 `Esc` 로 종료합니다. 발표 시간 타이머와 `N` 키로 표시하는 발표 노트, 장 목록을 제공합니다.

title: 슬라이드 작성
heading: 내보내기
text: **파일 → 내보내기**에서 PowerPoint(PPTX), PDF(발표용), 텍스트(노트 포함)를 선택합니다. 내용이 잘릴 우려가 있는 장, 근거 확인이 필요한 장, 미해결 검토 메모가 있으면 내보내기 전에 안내합니다. **대본 복사**로 슬라이드 본문과 발표 노트를 한 번에 복사할 수 있습니다. 어두운 인상은 PPTX에만 적용되며 PDF는 밝은 배경으로 출력됩니다.

title: 슬라이드 작성
heading: 수정
text: "2번 장을 더 간결하게"와 같이 요청하면 해당 장만 다시 작성합니다. "20장으로 늘려 주세요", "사례 장을 추가해 주세요"처럼 구성을 바꾸는 요청은 구성을 다시 제안한 뒤 승인을 받습니다. 자세한 내용은 요청으로 수정을 참고하십시오. 문장을 직접 고치거나 장 순서를 바꾸려면 아티팩트 편집기를 사용하십시오.

title: Approving published chatbots
text: When a member publishes an agent as a chatbot, other members can use it at once. Opening it to people without an account — **anyone with the link** or **public** — waits for an administrator's approval. Handle these under the account menu's **Admin** → **Published chatbots**. A number appears on the menu while requests are waiting.

title: Approving published chatbots
heading: What you review
text:
Opening a request shows the version that would answer once approved:

- Instructions, the department and contact line, the greeting, the tools and checks it uses, the strict-local model it answers with
- The material and how many values in it look like personal details
- The publisher, the daily credit limit, and the history so far (requests, decisions, new versions)

**Approve** opens the requested audience and that version together. **Decline** needs a reason, which the publisher sees on their management page. A declined chatbot keeps answering its previous audience.

When a new version arrives on a chatbot open to people without an account, it is reviewed the same way. Until approved, the approved version answers.

title: Approving published chatbots
heading: Channel requests
text:
The publisher of a chatbot open by link or to everyone can ask for the **Embed on other sites**, **API** and **MCP** channels. A request appears in the same review queue as "Channel request", and the review shows the channels and sites asked for.

- **Approve** opens the channels asked for. An embedded chat shows only on the sites you approved; adding a site is reviewed again.
- **Close to people without an account** closes the embed, API and MCP channels too. From then on the embedded chat, the API and MCP are refused at once.
- The channels open now are listed under **Open channels** on the review screen.

title: Approving published chatbots
heading: Reading conversations
text: **Conversation access** on the review screen is for checking abuse reports only. The list and the conversations open after you give a reason, with personal details masked. The date and reason go to the audit log and to the publisher's dashboard (**Administrator reads**). Conversations through an API or MCP key are marked "API/MCP key".

title: Approving published chatbots
heading: Closing and pausing
text:
| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Close to people without an account | Returns it to members only. Visitors without an account cannot open it from their next request |
| Pause / Reopen | Stops or resumes questions from every visitor |
| Close chatbot | Nobody but the publisher can open it |

Every action needs a reason and is recorded in the audit log. Reading a published chatbot's conversations for an abuse review also needs a reason and is recorded.

title: Approving published chatbots
heading: Operating notes
text:
- Visitors without an account are told apart by a browser cookie; per-address limits per minute and per day, and a daily cap on new visitors and conversations per address, guard against abuse. The address comes from the `X-Forwarded-For` the proxy in front sends, so narrow `KCHAT_TRUSTED_PROXIES` on the web container to the actual proxy.
- Questions answered at once by published chatbots across the organization stay under a cap (16 by default); the rest wait briefly and, if no turn comes, are told the chatbot is busy.

title: Administrator guide
text:
When you sign in with an administrator account, a **Manage** item appears in the account menu. The first account to sign up holds administrator rights.

| Screen | What it does |
|---|---|
| Users · Credits | Approve and reject sign-ups, suspend, edit details, monthly credits, allowed models, key management, review of shared processes and skills |
| Usage | Usage by period, by model, and by user, CSV, storage space |
| Published chatbots | Approve link and external publishing and channels (other sites, API, MCP), close or pause, abuse-check viewing |
| Security · Audit | The **Policy** tab (personal data protection, internal material, safe model, blocked topics, idle sign-out, retention period) and the **Audit log** tab |
| Feedback & issues | Read bug reports, feature requests and questions from users, set the assignee and status, reply |
| System | The **Proxy · Models · Routing · Features · Branding · Mail · Sign-up · Connector catalogue** tabs |
| Performance | One-screen dashboard of verdicts, key figures, GPU nodes and model servers; each item opens trends and details for the host, models, a node or a server |

title: Administrator guide
heading: Order of initial setup
text:
1. **System → Proxy**: Enter the model gateway address and master key, then check the connection. Until this is set, no models are available to use.
2. **System → Features**: Enable the features you will use and test the connection to each feature integration address (web search, document import, code execution, deep research, speech transcription, material search, text from scans (OCR)).
3. **System → Sign-up**: Set the sign-up method and the allowed email domains, and enable email verification if you have a mail server.
4. **System → Mail**: Set up SMTP if you need password reset and verification mail.
5. **System → Branding**: Set the service name, logo, and contact address.
6. **Security · Audit → Policy**: Designate the strict-local safe model and decide how personal data is protected.
7. **System → Routing**: Decide whether to use Auto mode.
8. **Users · Credits**: Process the accounts waiting for approval.

For the details of each item, see Users and credits, Policy and routing, Approving published chatbots, and System settings.

title: Policy and routing
text: This screen sets the level of personal data protection, the audit record, and automatic model switching (Auto).

title: Policy and routing
heading: Policy settings
text:
| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Personal data masking | Always masks national ID numbers, card numbers, phone numbers, and email addresses in every request, and stores them masked. The original cannot be sent |
| Personal data protection for external models | In Chat, asks the user to choose when personal data is detected for a model that may switch to an external provider |
| strict-local safe model | The model that "Switch to a safe local model" sends to. Only chat models the gateway declares as strict-local are candidates. **If you leave it empty**, users see a notice that there is no safe model |
| Internal material stays strict-local | A request carrying attachments, project files or memory is answered by the strict-local twin of the same model, and the conversation never moves to an external model afterwards. Without a twin, the safe model answers. Without that, the request is refused |
| Allow sending the original outside | Whether users may ignore the warning and send. Not possible while the masking policy is on |
| Intent-based filter + topics to block | Refuses the request without using credits and records it in the audit log |
| Automatic sign-out when idle | In minutes. 0 turns it off |
| Conversation retention period | In days. Once the period is up, the conversation body is deleted (applied retroactively, with the number deleted shown). Records and usage remain |

If the server cannot read the policy, it blocks sending in Chat, reports, and slide decks for safety (503).

In an environment where every model runs on organization servers, **Personal data protection for external models** has little effect. An organization model that is not declared strict-local is treated as a model that may switch to an external provider, so a warning appears. Declare strict-l

title: Policy and routing
heading: Audit log
text: Time, account, action, target, and access location. The log covers sign-ins, failures, approvals, suspensions, permission changes, setting changes, key issuance, discards, password resets, token reuse detection, and more. Search by account, action, or IP. It cannot be edited or deleted from the screen.

title: Policy and routing
heading: Auto routing
text:
- **Auto · Cost saving** — an on/off switch, the difficulty classification model (free strict-local only), and up to 3 saving models in priority order. A saving model is used only when its output price is lower than the quality model the user chose, its data boundary is no wider, and its context length is sufficient. In an environment where every model is free, there is nothing to save, so it does not run.
- **Auto · Quality first** — an on/off switch and up to 3 upgrade models.
- **Structuring stage model** — The model that sets the outline for a report or slide deck. If you leave it empty, it is the same as the writing model.

The default model per screen is not an administrator setting. It sits under **each user's Settings → Preferences**. Administrators only restrict the allowed models per user.

title: System settings
text: The **System** screen in the Manage menu is made up of eight tabs. Saved changes apply at once, without a restart.

title: System settings
heading: Proxy
text: The model gateway (LiteLLM) address and master key (stored encrypted, never shown again), **Connection test** (confirms n models), **Refresh model list**, and revert to the environment variable values. If models are listed as hidden for lack of price information, enter the model prices in the gateway settings.

title: System settings
heading: Models
text:
Decides which model does which job when the user has not chosen one. The values in the server's `.env` file are used once, at installation; after that, what is saved here takes precedence.

- **Default model for each screen**: chat, report, slides, image, audio and video. Chat and image must be chosen, and so must audio and video when the instance serves any. Left empty, report and slides follow the chat default. Price never picks a default: without a usable image, audio or video default, that screen makes nothing until the user picks a model, and says so. A model the user chose always comes first, and an agent with no model of its own follows the screen's default.
- **Side-work models**: the model for titles, memories and summaries, the code-writing model and its fallback. These read the conversation, so only models this instance runs itself (self-hosted) can be chosen. In a strict-local conversation the strict-local version of the chosen model does the work.
- **Thinking**: whether self-hosted and external models reason before answering. On makes judgements more exact but adds tens of seconds to minutes to each call. Both are off by default.

The **planning model** for reports and slides and Auto's **classifier model** are on the **Routing** tab.

### Self-hosted models of the default install

The defaults use two models the organization runs itself. Each is registered in the gateway under two names. A `local/` model runs on the organization's servers first, but an external fallback may answer when it fails, so it is treated as outside the data boundary. A `strict-local/` model never leaves, and it is the only route for internal material.

| Model | Jobs |
|---|---|
| `qwen3.8-27b` | Default report and slides model, code model |
| `qwen3.8-flash` | Default chat model,

title: System settings
heading: Routing
text: The routing settings are described in Policy and routing.

title: System settings
heading: Features
text:
- **Features to use**: Turn reports, slide decks, images, and audio/video on and off. Chat is always on. Disabling one removes it from the menu, and the server refuses new conversations for it as well. Images and video work in practice only if the gateway has those models. If you enable them without a model, the user screen shows a notice that generation is not possible.
- **Feature integration**: One feature server address, or an address per feature (web search · document import · code execution · deep research · speech transcription · material search · text from scans (OCR)). **Connection test** individually and for all of them. Setting a speech transcription address enables dictation and reading audio and video files. With a material search (indexing) address, agent material and conversation attachments are searched by vector (word search only without it).
- **Text from scans (OCR)**: Reads the text of scanned PDF pages and document photos. Set whether it is on, how pages are read (OCR engine + vision model · OCR engine only · vision model only), the vision model, and the most pages read in one document (300 by default). Only a strict-local model that reads pictures can be chosen as the vision model; any other is refused. With both, the engine reads first and only pages with a low score or a table are read again by the vision model; where the two differ, the page is marked “to check”. Without an OCR engine address, PDF pages are not read and only photos are read by the vision model. Pages read appear in usage as “n pages read” (0 credits).

The safe search level and blocked domains for web search are set on the search server. For details, see the backend (KloudChat-LLM) documentation. By default, safe search is off.

title: System settings
heading: Branding
text: The service name, the contact address (used by the mail link on the waiting screen; the first administrator's address if left empty), and the logo (PNG, JPG, WebP, up to 2MB, no SVG, with revert to default). Changing the service name also changes the browser tab icon to the matching initials.

title: System settings
heading: Mail
text: The SMTP host, port, security, account, and sender address, the service address (for mail links, with **Use the current address**), and **Send a test**. Once it is set, a password reset link appears on the sign-in screen and you can turn on email verification.

title: System settings
heading: Sign-up
text:
- **Sign-up method**: Use after approval / Use immediately / Not accepted. The value chosen on this screen overrides the `SIGNUP_MODE` environment variable.
- **Email domains allowed to sign up**: Several, separated by commas. Subdomains have to be listed separately.
- **Email verification**: Not effective without a mail server.
- **Monthly credits for new accounts**: granted at sign-up or approval. You can change it for each account when approving.

title: System settings
heading: Connector catalogue
text: The MCP servers people can install from **Customize** › **Connectors**. **Add entry** takes a name, slug, transport (run a command over stdio, HTTP or SSE), the command or address, environment variables and surfaces. Write tool addresses as placeholders such as `${TOOLS_STT_URL}`. Pick a **variable that gets the gateway key** and `TOOLS_GATEWAY_KEY` is added only while that variable is the chosen tool's address (this is how YouTube transcription calls speech-to-text). Stored values are never shown again; type one only to replace it. Servers that run as a command can only be added here. Turn off **Show in the list** (목록에 보이기) and the entry leaves the members' list but can still be installed, and what is installed keeps working (the admin list marks it Hidden). Turn off **Enabled** and nobody can install it anew. Turn on **Built in** (기본 제공) and the entry is installed at once for every active member, and for everyone who signs up or is approved later (the admin list marks it Built in). Members can switch a built-in connector off but cannot remove it. An entry that needs each person's credentials cannot be built in. Time, YouTube transcription and Deep research are built in.

title: System settings
heading: Management items outside the System tab
text:
- The **Usage** screen: charts by period, by model, by screen, and by user, CSV export, and storage space (disk usage, orphan file cleanup, and automatic cleanup from the oldest when it fills up).
- **Theme**: An administrator can **provide a theme to every user** (shared, read only).
- **Store**: Agents published by an administrator account carry an **Official** badge; skills carry the name of whoever shared them. Built-in skills start as skills of the first administrator account, shared with everyone. Administrators can edit them or stop sharing them in **Customize** › **Skills** like any other skill, and an edited skill is not overwritten by a newer version (unedited ones, and users' unedited copies, follow newer versions). Built-in skills hidden from the lists (kept only as parts) show to administrators only with **Show hidden** (숨김 포함).
- **Performance** screen: first-token and full-answer latency and error rate per model, turns in progress, API replica, host and GPU metrics, with items past their thresholds flagged as warning or overload. The first screen is a dashboard with the verdict, key figures and the GPU node and model server tables; clicking a figure or a table row opens the host or model trends, or the detail screen of one node or server. The thresholds are set with the API's `PERF_*` environment variables.
- The trusted proxy range, the file size limit, and similar settings are configured through environment variables rather than the screen. See `docs/configuration.md` in the repository.

title: Users and credits
text: This is the **Users · Credits** screen in the Manage menu. The top of the screen summarizes the total number of users, the number waiting for approval, this month's usage and allocation, and the next refill date. Below it are tabs by status (All, Waiting for approval, Active, Suspended) and a search by name and email.

title: Users and credits
heading: Approving sign-ups
text: If the sign-up method is **Use after approval**, new accounts build up as waiting for approval and the account menu shows "N waiting for approval". Press **Approve** on a row to approve the account immediately with the default plan credits. The model gateway user and key are created at that point. Handle accounts you will not approve with **Reject**. An account that has not completed email verification shows a **Mail not verified** badge. Approving the account counts the verification as complete. Selecting several at once is not supported, so you have to approve each account individually.

title: Users and credits
heading: Management items per user
text:
| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| Credits | Change the monthly limit. The gateway budget is adjusted by the same amount |
| Model restriction | The models this account can use. Leave it empty for all of them. It applies to API keys too |
| Edit details | Name and email, **Reset password** (a random password; saving it signs out all of the user's sessions) |
| Key management | Reissue the gateway key (the existing key is discarded at once) or replace it. List and delete the API keys the user created |
| Suspend / Unsuspend | Reversible, and a record is kept |
| Delete | Deletes conversations, projects, artifacts, memory, credit records, and the gateway key. You choose whether to delete the uploaded files and the generated image and video files from disk |

title: Users and credits
heading: Sharing review
text:
Two review queues sit at the bottom of the page. Approve, or reject with a reason that the author sees as written.

- **Process review**: A custom process or bundle that exports a file, has another model review, or calls another agent is used by others only after approval.
- **Skill review**: A skill with uploaded scripts is copied by others only after approval. The scripts run only in the code execution sandbox.

title: Users and credits
heading: Credit policy
text: The credits of an approved account reset to the allocation on the 1st of each month and do not carry over. In an environment that runs only free models, credits are not consumed, and the limit applies in practice only when external models or the image and video features are enabled.

title: Users and credits
heading: Cleaning up accounts
text: Delete accounts created for verification or load testing once you are done with them. If you do not delete them, they are counted in the usage totals as well.

title: API and coding tool integration
text: You can call the models your organization runs from your own code or from a coding tool. The account menu has two screens, **API integration** and **AI agent integration**.

title: API and coding tool integration
heading: API integration
text:
1. Issue a key under Settings → **API keys**.
2. Follow the examples shown on the screen. Examples are provided for the OpenAI SDK, streaming, the LiteLLM SDK (`openai/` prefix), curl, and embeddings.
3. For the model name, use **the id shown in the model list** exactly as it appears.

```bash
# Linux / macOS, OpenAI-compatible

```

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
$env:OPENAI_BASE_URL = "https:///llm/v1"
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY = ""
```

Requests sent with a key reach the usage screen and this month's credits within a few minutes, and appear as **API keys** in the by-screen breakdown. Requests to free models are counted as requests too. Any allowed-model restriction set on the account applies to the key in the same way.

title: API and coding tool integration
heading: Reasoning effort
text:
Models that reason let you set how much they think. Send `reasoning_effort` in the OpenAI format, `reasoning.effort` in the Responses API, or `thinking` in the Anthropic format.

```bash
curl "$OPENAI_BASE_URL/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "z-ai/glm-5.3-flash", "reasoning_effort": "low",
       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]}'
```

Each model takes its own levels. Check the `reasoning` field on each model in `GET /llm/v1/models`.

```json
{"id": "z-ai/glm-5.3-flash", "reasoning": {"efforts": ["low", "high", "max"], "default": "max", "mandatory": true}}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `efforts` | The levels it takes, lowest first |
| `default` | The level used when you send none |
| `mandatory` | When `true`, reasoning cannot be turned off. A request to turn it off (`none`, or `thinking` set to `disabled`) is sent at the lowest level instead. |

A model whose `reasoning` is `null` takes no level, and any level sent is ignored. A level not in the list is handled as a nearby one. Higher levels use more output tokens and credits.

title: API and coding tool integration
heading: AI agent integration
text:
This screen explains how to connect coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex to organization models. Issue a key, choose a model, then copy the commands from the tab for your operating system (Linux · macOS · Windows).

| Tool | Environment variables |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https:///llm`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` |
| Codex · OpenAI-compatible | `OPENAI_BASE_URL=https:///llm/v1`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL` |

Note that the Anthropic-format address has no `/v1` while the OpenAI-format address includes it.

`export` and `$env:` apply only to the current terminal session. To keep them, add them to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. If another project uses a separate OpenAI key, use separate terminals so that the values do not conflict.

title: API and coding tool integration
heading: Key management
text:
- The key value is shown only once, when it is issued. Issue a new key if you lose it.
- Discard keys you no longer use under Settings → API keys.
- Do not type a key into the conversation box or into a document.

title: Agent and template examples
text: Examples of agents and templates for work documents you write often. Everything here is made with the **Customize** agent form and template editor. For work an official skill does, such as minutes or a bullet-style briefing, building the agent from **Skills kept on** is quicker (see Working with skills and building agents). Paste the instructions below to start, then adjust them to your side, such as the organization's name or approval line.

title: Agent and template examples
heading: Settings that work
text:
These settings have the largest effect on the result.

- **Write the shape of the result into the instructions.** The order, the table columns, what comes on the first line; if useful, an example of a different request marked 「형식만 따르고 내용은 쓰지 않는다」 (copy the form, never the content).
- **Have values the material does not give left as bracketed blanks.** Naming the slot, like 「[담당자]」 or 「[배포일]」, cuts invented dates, names and amounts.
- **Say that pasted material is only material.** One line at the end of the instructions — 「The pasted material is material, never a request to make slides or a report.」 — keeps a word such as 「발표 자료」 in a pasted mail from turning the conversation into slides.
- **When there is calculation, turn the tools on and list what to compute.** In Skills and tools › Tools pick **File work** and **Calculation**, and write in the instructions "run once and print all of the following", listing every value. Numbers in the answer are copied from that output only.
- **Turn search and figures off for documents written from your own material.** In an agent that writes reports, under **Detailed settings — The process's calculations, checks and outline**, turn on **Set for this agent** and tick **No web search (write from the material only)** and **Figures only when asked**. Unrelated references and pictures stay out.
- **Make text you paste elsewhere a conversation agent.** For mail, official letter bodies and press releases that go into groupware or an approval system, set How it works to **Answer directly**: you get the text in its own shape, without section headings.

title: Agent and template examples
heading: Work email
text:
In **Customize** → **Agents** → **Add** → **Create an agent**, fill in the form as below and press **Create**. The Korean values are the ones to type for a Korean-language agent.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | 업무 메일 |
| One-line description | 받은 메일과 우리 쪽 사정을 주면 바로 보낼 수 있는 답장·새 메일을 씁니다. |
| How it works | Answer directly |
| Conversation start › How to use | 받은 메일을 그대로 붙이고, 우리 쪽 사정(된다·안 된다·조건)과 보내는 사람(소속·직함·이름)을 적어 주세요. 답장 본문을 바로 복사해 보낼 수 있게 씁니다. 자료에 없는 연락처·날짜는 [전화번호]처럼 대괄호 빈칸으로 둡니다. |
| Conversation start › Conversation starters | 아래 메일에 답장 써 줘. 우리 쪽 상황: / 이 메일 정중하게 거절하는 답장 써 줘. 이유는 / 협조 요청 메일 새로 써 줘. 받는 사람: |
| Skills and tools › Tools | Pick, and leave every tool unticked |
| Advanced › Variety | 0.3 |

**Instructions**:

```text
You write work emails in Korean (in the sender's language if the received mail is in another language) that the person can copy and send as is. The reader is the counterpart named in the received mail.

Output, in this order and nothing else:
1. 「제목: RE: <원래 제목>」 on one line (for a new mail, a short specific subject).
2. The body: greeting with the recipient's name and title (「정다은 선임연구원님, 안녕하세요.」), one line saying who is writing (소속·이름), then the answer.
3. Closing line and signature block (소속 / 직함 이름 / [전화번호] / [이메일] — brackets for anything not given).

How to write the body:
- Answer every question or request in the received mail, in the order the mail asked them. When there are two or more, use short bold headings or a numbered list (1. 일정 2. 발표자 3. 자료 4. 주차) so the reader can tick them off.
- Lead with the answer (가능합니다 / 어렵습니다), then the condition or reason in one sentence. If our side cannot fully meet a request (a later date, fewer cars, a shorter time), say so plainly, give the alternative from our notes, and add one short line

title: Agent and template examples
heading: Official letter draft
text:
In **Customize** → **Agents** → **Add** → **Create an agent**, fill in the form as below and press **Create**. The Korean values are the ones to type for a Korean-language agent.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | 공문 초안 |

text:
A template fixes a document's structure: head fields, contents, required tables and writing rules. Make it under **Output shape** › Template › **New template**.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Start from a built-in template | Blank template |
| Name | 공모사업 계획서 |
| Group | 업무 |
| One-line description | 지자체·기관 공모 신청용 사업계획서 · 필요성 근거, 성과지표 표, 프로그램·일정·추진체계·예산 표 |
| What to bring | 사업명·신청 기관·기간 / 필요성 근거(통계) / 프로그램 내용과 규모 / 예산 항목 / 성과 목표 / 추진 체계·협력 기관 |
| Document format › Document type name | 사업계획서 |
| Document format › Head fields | 사업명 / 신청 기관 / 사업 기간 / 총사업비 / 사업 책임자 |
| Document format › Numbered list | 1. / 1.1 |
| Document format › Head layout | Field table under the title |
| Checks | Grounding check (근거 대조) |
| Detailed settings › How it writes | No web search (write from the material only), Figures only when asked, Fixed outline (write exactly these sections) |
| Detailed settings › Contents | 사업 개요 / 추진 배경 및 필요성 / 사업 목표 및 성과지표 / 세부 프로그램 / 추진 일정 / 추진 체계 / 예산 계획 / 기대 효과 |
| Detailed settings › Required tables | Column names 「항목, 금액, 비율, 산출 근거」, section it belongs in 「예산」 |
| Detailed settings › Review rules | 심사위원에게 승인·채택을 권고하는 문장(신청자가 아닌 심사자 시점)이 있으면 찾는다. / 사람 수를 소수점으로 적은 곳(예: 22.5명)이 있으면 찾는다. |

**How to write it › Instructions**:

```text
Build this document as a 공모사업 계획서 (an application a public funder's 심사위원 scores). Write as the applicant (「~하고자 합니다」「~를 운영합니다」), never as a reviewer recommending approval.

Sections, in this order:
1. 사업 개요 — two or three sentences: who is served, what is done, the headline numbers (people, sessions).
2. 추진 배경 및 필요성 — the material's statistics as a table (근거 | 수치 | 시사점), then why this program answers them.
3. 사업 목표 및 성과지표 — a table (성과 지표 | 목표 | 측정 방법). Measurement methods the material does not give stay as brackets like 「[측정 시점]」.

| Conversation start › How to use | 사업명·신청 기관·기간, 필요성 근거가 되는 통계, 프로그램별 대상·규모, 예산 항목, 성과 목표, 추진 체계를 메모로 붙여 주세요. 자료에 없는 단가·측정 방법은 대괄호 빈칸으로 남깁니다. |
| Conversation start › Conversation starters | 아래 메모로 공모사업 계획서 써 줘. / 시 공모사업 신청서의 사업계획 부분을 써 줘. |

**Instructions**:

```text
You write the 사업계획서 of a public grant application from the applicant's notes. The reader is a 심사위원 scoring necessity, feasibility, budget soundness and measurable outcomes. Write as the applicant. Every number comes from the notes; anything a 심사위원 would expect but the notes do not give (unit prices, measurement timing, names) is a bracketed blank like 「[단가]」. Do not search the web or cite outside sources.

Shape of every section: first its table, then at most three one-line bullets; never a paragraph longer than two sentences. Do not derive new figures (per-person cost, per-unit rent, totals of people across programs, monthly splits) — the reviewer only needs the material's own numbers and the budget ratios. The schedule is three phases (준비 / 운영 / 평가) by month range, without inventing which cohort runs in which month. Partners' roles are only what the notes say (MOU 예정 → 「협약 예정」). Rented equipment (임차) is returned, not reused.
```

- Satisfaction as a table with the scale (「5점 만점」); problems as a table (문제

title: Agent and template examples
heading: Checking after you make one
text:
- Open a conversation with one starter and one real memo. Check that numbers, dates and names match the material and that values the material lacks were left as bracketed blanks.
- If two runs on the same memo differ a lot, write the shape (order, table columns) more concretely in the instructions.
- You can also keep a good conversation with **⋯** › **Save as agent** on the artifact card (Agents and skills).

title: Agents and skills
text:
An agent is an assistant with a role, instructions, tools, and material already configured. You make your own for work you do often, such as English conversation practice, meeting minutes, or paper review, or import one a colleague has published.

Field-by-field examples are in Agent and template examples.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Starting a conversation with an agent
text:
**+** → **Agents** in the composer and **Run** in the agent list both start a new conversation with that agent.

Jobs such as minutes or a bullet-point report are **official skills**. For minutes, on the report screen choose **+** → **Skills** → **회의록 작성** (Meeting minutes) in the composer, attach or paste the recording transcript or notes, and send 「회의록으로 정리해 주세요」. Work you do often becomes an agent of your own with that skill kept on (Working with skills and building agents).

- The first screen of the conversation shows the agent's **How to use** text and its **opening prompts**, up to six of them. Select an opening prompt to send it as it is.
- An agent conversation uses the model, tools, and material set on the agent. When material is registered, the model searches it with the **Find in files** tool. Not all of the material is sent with every request.
- Within the same project, other conversations reference the conclusions that the agent left through **Shared notes**.

There are no built-in agents. Jobs such as Regulations and procedures, Bullet-style briefing, Compare and decide, Extract and tally and Minutes are done by official skills of the same names. The built-in agents for these jobs do not show in the lists or among the base processes, but conversations with them, copies you took and chatbots published from them keep working.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Creating an agent
text:
**Customize** → **Agents** → **Add** → **Create an agent**. **Create agent** at the end of the composer's **+** → **Agents** list opens it too.

The form runs from top to bottom like this:

1. The **name**, the **one-line description** and the **instructions** (the role and rules the agent always follows). Instructions for one surface only go under a line `[채팅에서]` (chat), `[보고서에서]` (report) or `[슬라이드에서]` (slides); what comes before the first such line applies everywhere.
2. **How it works** (진행 과정): Answer directly · Start from a base process · Set it up yourself (advanced) (see "How it works" below).
3. **Extra work**: the bundle checkboxes (see "Bundles"). Set it up yourself has none; you build steps instead.
4. **Detailed settings — The process's calculations, checks and outline**: shown only for an agent that writes reports (see "Detailed settings and your own templates").
5. **Missing-information questions**: what to ask before writing when the material lacks it; up to four at a time while "Ask for missing information first" is on. A * marks a field you must fill.
6. Under **More settings**: **Template & theme**, **Conversation start**, **Sources**, **Skills and tools**, **Advanced** and **Share** (see "Template & theme and sources").

A new agent is saved only when you press **Create**. The instructions go with every conversation of that agent, so write only the role and rules it should always follow. An agent works when you open a conversation and ask; it never runs by itself on a schedule such as weekly, nor re-summarises its sources.

The enable toggle pauses an agent. Deleting it also deletes its sources, index and custom order; past conversations stay. The overview says how it works in one line, with the ticked bundles behind **Show details**.

title: Agents and skills
heading: How it works
text:
Pick one of three under **How it works** in the create-agent form. A new agent and its process are saved together: if the process is refused, no agent is made and the form stays as it was.

- **Answer directly**: answers the request right away. An agent that answers in the chat makes no file (DOCX, HWPX, PDF).
- **Start from a base process**: follows the working order of a built-in agent (Bullet-style briefing, Minutes, Compare and decide, …). When no base process can be picked this option is hidden; it shows only on an agent that already started from one (which keeps it). A new agent does the same job with **Answer directly** plus **Skills kept on** and bundles. To get a file, set **Advanced** › first screen to **Report** and tick **Export a file when done** under Finish.
- **Set it up yourself (advanced)**: pick questions, calculations, checks, reviews, other agents and exports one step at a time. It starts with one "This agent" step. Choose **Report (document)** or **Chat (answer)** under **What this agent makes**; an export step works only with Report (document). With Chat (answer) and an export step, the button under the warning switches that field to Report (document), and **Undo** on the notice switches it back. Presentation has no custom order.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Bundles
text:
A bundle groups a few things an agent does before and after writing. Each bundle is one checkbox under **Extra work** in the create-agent form; **Details** opens its items as checkboxes.

| Bundle | Items |
|---|---|
| Prepare before writing | Ask for missing information first · Work out dates ahead · Work out amounts and totals ahead |
| Review after writing | Check everything against the material (accept numbers only from tool output · check job titles and product names too) · Format checks · Fix what is off and check again |
| Finish | Strip stock phrases · Export a file when done (DOCX, PDF, HWPX or MD) |

- **Get a file**: with **Finish** ticked, a separate **Export a file when done** checkbox shows under it; tick it and pick the format beside it (HWPX for 공문-type documents, else DOCX). The base processes come with Finish ticked and export off. Export works only in a process that writes a document.
- On the report screen, date and amount calculations, format checks and fix-and-check-again always happen in report writing ("Always done"). The chat screen has no format checks and no export.
- Base processes are built from the same bundles: Minutes is Prepare + Review + Finish (export off). The **회의록 작성** skill and **Minutes** template carry those checks.
- **Your own bundles**: **Customize** → **Agents** → **Add** → **Create a bundle**, or **Save this order as a bundle** in a custom order. They appear under Extra work in all your agents; edit and share them from **Manage bundles**.
- Sharing works like skills (Only me · Everyone). A bundle or custom order that exports files, has another model review or calls another agent reaches others only once an administrator approves it under **Process review**; base processes and built-in bundles are shared at once.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Template & theme and sources
text:
These sit under **More settings** in the create-agent form.

- **Template & theme**: pick the **template** (the structure of a report or deck) and the **theme** (colours, typeface, writing style). **New template** under the template makes your own; **Manage themes** under the theme opens Settings › Themes. An agent started from a base process uses the base's template when the template is left empty ("The base's template"), and that template sets the document format. The **Document format** field shows only for a report-writing agent on Answer directly or Set it up yourself.
- **Conversation start**: **How to use** (shown on the conversation's first screen) and **Conversation starters** (one per line, up to six).
- **Sources**: files and web addresses the agent searches and cites (**Attach file**, **Add URL**). They are not sent whole with every conversation; the agent looks things up when needed. A URL stores the page as it was when added and does not follow later changes. Sources are not re-read or re-summarised on a schedule, and an agent never runs by itself at set times; it works when you open a conversation and ask.
- **Skills and tools** and **Advanced** (screens, first screen, model, output language, web search default, variety, colour, use memory). Adding a screen while no first screen is chosen makes it the first screen. Keeping on a skill that works only on reports or slides (회의록 작성, 개조식 보고, …) sets the first screen to that screen when none is chosen, and a line under the skills says where each one works. **Share**: **Only me** or **Everyone**, and when shared, **Let others take and edit it** or **Let others take it but keep the content private**.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Output language, web search and memory
text:
These are under **Advanced** in the agent form.

- **Output language**: pick **Auto (the request's language)**, 한국어, English, 日本語 or 中文, or type a language name under **Type one in**. Once set, every answer, report and slide deck of this agent is written in that language, whatever language the question or the material is in. A turn that asks for another language itself ("영어로", "in Korean") follows that request. A published bot answers in it too.
- **Web search default**: whether the composer's web search starts on **Auto**, **Always** or **Off** in a new conversation with this agent. You can change it per turn in the composer. With **Off**, a question about current facts is not searched first (asking "search for it" still searches). A turn sent through the API without a web search setting uses this value.
- **Use memory**: when off, your memories are not added to this agent's conversations, and those conversations create no automatic memories or shared notes.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Detailed settings and your own templates
text:
An agent that writes reports can turn on **Set for this agent** under **Detailed settings — The process's calculations, checks and outline** below the process and change what its template sets, starting from the template's values. Turned off, the template's (or document format's) settings apply as they are.

- **Calculate before writing**: built-in calculations such as dates, quote totals, staffing, total cost per option, must-haves and weighted scores, career periods; and the **date basis** (the material's date or the meeting day).
- **How it writes**: no web search, figures only when asked, a fixed outline.
- **Structure rules**: sections in order, required tables (columns), summary lines at the top, bullet style, page limit. Checked by code.
- **Review rules**: rules in your own words. After writing, a judge model shows the sentences that break them; nothing is rewritten.
- **Calculation checks**, **Judged checks**, **Value fixes**, **Fill in what is missing**: built-in checks and repair steps attached by name.
- **When the material disagrees**: left empty, the writing says which value it used and why.

Make your own document template with **New template** under **Template & theme** › Template (or in the template picker). **Start from a built-in template** fills in all of its settings: the document format's head fields, numbering, head layout, bullet style and closing, the instructions, genre rule, checklist, missing-information questions, checks and detailed settings. An uploaded DOCX/HWPX sample document is read by the writing model as reference. The theme's colours and fonts draw it. Shared with **Everyone**, others can pick it; only its maker edits it. Your templates appear under **My templates** in the template picker.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Save as agent
text:
Keep a conversation that went well as an agent. **Save as agent** in the **⋯** menu of an artifact card, or of the report or slides panel, opens the create-agent screen filled in. Nothing is made until you press **Save**.

- The **instructions** start with "Settled in this conversation" (the reader, the length, what to always include …). Only your own messages are read, by the model the conversation used. A strict-local conversation is summarised only by its strict-local model and nothing leaves. The other fields fill in first; the instructions are added when the summary is done. If it cannot be made, the banner says so and offers **Retry**.
- The conversation's template, theme, skills, base process and bundles are filled in, and you choose whether to save the conversation's files as sources.
- A privately shared agent's instructions are never copied.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Workspace store
text:
**Shared agents** under **Explore** on **Customize** → **Agents** shows, with their makers' names, the agents other users have published and the agents published to members as chatbots. An **Official** badge marks an item published by an administrator. Select **Add** to create a **copy** in your own list.

- A copy does not include the original author's knowledge files. Its process and bundles come along (a custom order still waiting for approval stays behind; the copy uses the base process).
- A copy of an agent published as "contents stay private" cannot be edited, and any change to the original applies to the copy as well.
- Other copies are managed independently, so a change to the original does not affect them.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Skills
text:
A skill is a working method kept on in a conversation: select up to three from **+** → **Skills** (again to turn one off). An **official skill** is added to your skills when picked. A skill brings its template, checks and questions.

- Use **Customize** → **Skills** to install a skill, stop using one, or build your own with a name, description, when to use it, steps, required tools, and visibility. A published skill is listed in the store, and other users import it as a copy.
- **Customize › Skills › Add › Upload skill** takes a SKILL.md (.md) or a .zip/.skill file containing one, several at a time. A .md file needs YAML front matter with `name` and `description`; .md and .txt files under `resources/` are appended to the body under 「참고 자료」 (References). Before anything is saved, each file shows a preview and its security-scan findings (blocked or warning). Python scripts under `scripts/` are stored with the skill and run only in the code execution sandbox; other scripts (.sh, .js and the like) are left out. A published skill with scripts can be copied by others only after an administrator approves it under **Skill review**. The checks are heuristic and will not catch every risk. **Upload as draft** saves the skill switched off.
- A skill's **⋯ → Export (SKILL.md)** downloads your skill as a SKILL.md file. Sharing is refused while a skill contains key- or token-like strings or invisible direction-control characters.
- A skill that requires tools is enabled only when all of these hold: you are on the Chat screen, the model supports tool calling, and that tool is connected. When a condition is not met, the reason is shown.
- Skills you pick with **Choose skills** on a project's **Skills** tab appear first in that project's composer.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Tool skills on reports and slides
text: On the Report and Slides screens you can pick a skill that needs tools when the server does its work around the writing: it calculates or checks before or after, such as **Calculation and unit check**, **Date calculation** and **Quote calculation**. The picker shows "The server calculates and checks around the writing". Other skills that need tools can be picked only on the Chat screen.

title: Agents and skills
heading: Built-in skills
text:
Built-in skills are skills the administrator account made and shared with everyone. They appear under **Explore** in **Customize** › **Skills** as **By: Official**; **Add** puts a copy in your list (**Original: Official**). A copy follows the administrator's newer versions while you leave it unedited, and stays yours once you edit it. The checks agents and templates use (grounding check, asking for missing information and so on) run without adding anything.

The lists show the thirteen work skills (including Translation, Press release, Make an Excel file and Make a chart) under Official skills and **Grounding check** (근거 대조), **Ask for missing information** (빠진 정보 묻기), **Calculation and unit check** (계산·단위 검증), **Date calculation** (날짜 계산), **Quote calculation** (견적 계산), **Excel cleanup** (엑셀 정리), **PDF table → Excel** (PDF 표 → 엑셀) and **Mask personal information** (개인정보 가리기).

- **Excel cleanup** strips title, blank, total and note rows and records what it changed on a change-log sheet. Rows whose values are all the same are not removed, only marked 「중복 의심」 (suspected duplicate); ask for them to be removed if you want that.
- **PDF table → Excel** reads only PDFs whose text can be selected (text PDFs). Scanned PDFs (images) cannot be read.
- The other skills (copy, market research, proofreading, stock-phrase stripping, character-count fitting and so on) are not shown in the lists, the store and the pickers. They still run in bundles (such as Finish's stock-phrase stripping) and in conversations that used them, and the editors still let you pick them by name. Administrators see them with **Show hidden** (숨김 포함).

title: Conversation basics
text: On the home screen select **Chat**, enter a request, and press `Enter`. The answer is generated in real time. If you turn streaming off in settings, the answer appears all at once after it is complete.

title: Conversation basics
heading: Parts of an answer
text:
| Element | Details |
|---|---|
| Answered · N steps | The steps the answer went through. Reports and slides name what was done instead, such as "Wrote the report". Expand it to see steps such as using attachments, carrying over attachments from earlier turns, applying personalization settings, referring to memory, searching the web, reading documents, running code, and searching files. Files that were truncated or could not be read also appear here. |
| Processing detail badge | Shows whether Auto switched the model, whether personal data was masked, and which model actually answered. On mobile it collapses to "n processing details". |
| Usage line | Shows the model name, input and output tokens, and credits. Free models are marked **Free**. You can hide this line in Settings → Preferences. |
| Sources | When a web search runs, numbers in the form `[1]` appear in the text and a source list appears below it. |

Copy and rating (👍 · 👎) buttons sit below the answer.

title: Conversation basics
heading: Stopping and resuming generation
text: While an answer is being generated, the send button changes to ■ **Stop**. If you stop, the content generated so far is saved and usage is recorded as an estimate. Generation continues on the server even if you close or refresh the browser tab, so you can return later and see the finished answer.

title: Conversation basics
heading: When generation fails
text: The answer area shows **Retry** and **Another model** buttons. **Another model** applies a different model to that request only.

title: Conversation basics
heading: Editing a sent message
text: In Chat, select **Edit message** (the pencil icon) next to a message you sent. The composer shows **Editing · sending starts a new conversation; this one stays as it is** and fills in the original text and attachments. When you send the edited text, the answer is generated in a **new conversation** that copies everything before that message. The original conversation stays as it was. Use **Cancel edit** or `Esc` to stop editing. You cannot edit while an answer is being generated.

title: Conversation basics
heading: Keeping conversation context
text: Within the same conversation, earlier questions, answers, and attached files stay available. Short follow-ups such as "So what happens next?" or "Explain that in more detail" work fine. When the topic changes, press **New chat** in the sidebar. Earlier context does not mix in, so the answer is more accurate.

title: Conversation basics
heading: Dictating a request
text:
Use the 🎤 button in the composer. It appears only where the administrator has connected a **speech transcription** server. There are two ways to use it.

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| 🎤 button or `Ctrl+Shift+M` | The recording is converted to text and placed in the composer. Edit it, then send. |
| Hold `Space` in an empty composer and speak | On release the words are typed into the composer, not sent. Works only with **Hold Space to dictate** on under Settings → Preferences. |

Recordings are not stored. If there is no microphone or no permission, the message "Microphone is unavailable" appears.

title: Conversation basics
heading: Managing conversations
text:
- Use the `…` menu on a sidebar item to rename, pin, remove from a project, or delete. The title is generated automatically after the first answer.
- A new conversation with nothing sent is deleted automatically when you leave the screen.
- **Deleting a conversation also deletes the artifacts and share links created in it.** Projects and memory are kept.
- To tidy up several conversations at once, use the account menu → **Conversation history**. Usage and conversation history

title: Conversation basics
heading: Adjusting answer length
text: KloudChat answers are designed to lead with the conclusion and to skip introductions, repeated explanation, and closing summaries. If you need a more detailed answer, add conditions such as "in detail" or "include examples" to your request. You can also describe the length you want under **Answer style** in Personalization.

title: Publishing a chatbot
text: Publish an agent that answers in chat as a **chatbot**, and other people can ask it. A chatbot is fixed to the instructions, material and checks it had when published, and answers with this organization's strict-local models only. The credits it spends are its publisher's, and questions are handled under the same policy as if the publisher had typed them.

title: Publishing a chatbot
heading: Publishing
text:
The **Publish as a chatbot** button at the top of your agent's page. Before publishing you see:

- The strict-local model it will answer with. Without a strict-local model you can use, it cannot be published.
- What a chatbot does not use: your memory, personal settings, other files and projects, connectors, web search, documents and slides, skills. A chatbot uses only **material search** and **calculation**.
- Values in the material that look like personal details (mobile numbers, emails and so on). Remove or check them before publishing.

title: Publishing a chatbot
heading: Audience
text:
| Audience | Who uses it | Opens |
|---|---|---|
| Members | Members of this organization, signed in. Members see it as a **shared agent** | At once |
| Anyone with the link | Anyone with the address, without signing in. Listed nowhere | After an administrator approves |
| Public | Anyone, without signing in. Listed on the public chatbot page (`/b`) and may show up in search | After an administrator approves |

- Choosing a link or public audience needs a **daily credit limit**. When the day's spending reaches it, the chatbot stops until the next day.
- While the request waits, members can use the chatbot as usual. The request shows at the top of the management page, and **Withdraw request** takes it back.
- When a request is declined, the administrator's reason shows on the management page. The chatbot keeps answering its previous audience.
- Narrowing the audience (public → link → members) needs no approval and applies at once.

title: Publishing a chatbot
heading: Versions and approval
text:
After changing the agent, use **Versions** → **Publish new version** on the management page for the chatbot to pick it up. Roll back to an earlier version if something is wrong.

On a chatbot open to people without an account, a new version is also reviewed by an administrator before it answers. Until then the approved version keeps answering, and the new one shows as **Awaiting approval** in the version list. Rolling back to a version that was approved before applies at once.

title: Publishing a chatbot
heading: Channels: other sites, API, MCP
text:
A chatbot open to people without an account can also be reached through these channels besides its own page. Switch them under **Channels** on the dashboard's **Overview**. Switching one on opens once an administrator approves; switching off applies at once.

| Channel | What it does | Available at |
|---|---|---|
| Embed on other sites | Puts the chat on your own sites, such as your organization's homepage | Open to everyone |
| API | Calls the bot from your service or program, OpenAI-compatible | By link, open to everyone |
| MCP | Connects the bot as a tool in AI tools such as Claude | By link, open to everyone |

- **Embed on other sites**: list the sites (starting with `https://`, up to 10) and ask. Once approved, paste the one-line embed code before ``: a chat button appears in the corner and opens the chat (full screen on a phone). The chat shows only on approved sites, and inside them it always acts as a visitor without an account.
- **API and MCP**: on the dashboard's **API** tab, make a key that calls this bot only. A key is shown once, when it is made; keep it then. **Revoke** a key you no longer use and it stops at once.
  - Call the API at `/api/bots/v1/chat/completions` with the bot's address as `model`. Only checked answers go out, so with `stream` on the answer arrives once it is finished. Cited material is in `kloudchat.citations`.
  - Connect MCP at `/api/bots/mcp/` with the same key; it offers one tool, `ask`.
  - Questions through a key have per-minute and per-day limits for that key, and the daily credit cap and the bot's own limits still apply.
- The **API** tab and **Statistics** show questions by channel (bot page, other sites, API, MCP).
- When an administrator closes the outside audience, or the audience is narrowed, the channels it can no long

title: Publishing a chatbot
heading: What the publisher sees
text:
The management page (**Chatbot** → **Manage** on your agent's page) shows:

- **Statistics**: questions, conversations, visitors, frequent topics, unanswered questions (sentences with personal details masked), 👍👎.
- **Sent conversations**: only conversations a visitor sent with **Send to the maker**, personal details masked. With **Conversation access** on, conversations after the visitor's consent show too. Turn it on only for chatbots whose conversations are the work itself, such as counselling or complaints.
- **Allow copies** under **Settings**: off (locked) by default. Turn it on and members can take the chatbot, instructions included, as their own agent. Leave it off to keep the instructions to yourself.
- Visitors show as "Visitor ABC123" with only whether they signed in. **Block this visitor** on a sent conversation stops them from asking; unblock them under **Settings** → **Blocked visitors**.

When an administrator reads conversations to check abuse, the date and reason appear under **Administrator reads** on **Overview**.

When a chatbot stops (credits used up, paused by an administrator and so on) or an administrator decides a request, a number appears next to **Customize** in the sidebar.

title: Publishing a chatbot
heading: On a member's side
text:
A chatbot published to members (or to the public) shows to other members as an agent. There is no separate chatbot menu.

- It is listed under **Shared agents** in **Customize** → **Agents** → **Explore**, with its publisher's name. Agents shared with everyone sit in the same place, and an agent that is both shows once.
- In the composer, **+** → **Agents** lists it under **Shared agents**, below your own agents.
- **Use now** or its name opens a conversation on the chatbot page. Answers spend the publisher's credits.
- Chatbots are locked by default: members can only **Use now**. **Add** shows only on chatbots whose publisher turned on **Allow copies**; it copies the published version's instructions and settings as your own agent. Material (knowledge files) does not come along. Even with copies allowed, an agent whose maker keeps the instructions private cannot be copied. A locked chatbot shows a lock instead of **Add**.

title: Publishing a chatbot
heading: On the visitor's side
text:
- Visitors read the notice before their first question. It states how long conversations are kept and whether the publisher can read them.
- A visitor without an account continues their conversations only through this browser's cookie. Clearing cookies loses past conversations. They cannot upload files or download artifacts.
- Questions are limited per person, per address (visitors without an account) and per chatbot, per minute and per day. Lower the limits under **Settings** → **Limits** on the management page.
- Conversations are deleted once the retention period (30 days by default) passes after the last question.

title: Connectors
text: A connector is an external tool (an MCP server) that the model can call. Install one from **Customize** → **Connectors**, and turn it on or off from **+** → **Connectors** in the composer. The on or off state applies to your **whole account**.

title: Connectors
heading: Built-in connectors
text:
Connectors the administrator marks **Built in** are installed for everyone and appear under **My connectors** with a Built in badge. If you do not use one, switch it off, or switch off single tools. A built-in connector cannot be removed; one you switched off comes back as it was when you switch it on again.

| Connector | What it does |
|---|---|
| Time | Looks up the current time and date. Available in Chat, Reports, and Slides. |
| YouTube transcription | Fetches a video's captions from its address, or transcribes the audio when there are none. Available in Chat and Reports. |
| Deep research | Searches and reads the web over several rounds and sums up what it found. It can take minutes. Available in Chat and Reports. |

The catalogue shows only the entries the administrator made visible in the connector catalogue. A connector hidden from the list keeps working for anyone who already installed it.

title: Connectors
heading: Adding a server directly
text: If you already use an MCP server, connect it with **Add server directly**. Enter the name, the transport (stdio, http, or sse), the run command or endpoint address, the environment variables, and the authentication method. Environment variables and credentials are not shown again after saving.

title: Connectors
heading: Tool permissions
text:
Set each tool on or off in the connector detail screen. A **write** tool that changes data asks for confirmation before it runs. Content returned by a connector is treated as external input, so any instructions inside it are not executed.

The more tools you enable, the less likely the model is to choose the right one, so enable only the tools you actually use.

title: Attaching files
text: Attach files from **+** → **Attach files or photos** in the composer, and the model answers from their content. You can attach several files at once, and you can drag and drop them or paste them in. The Images and Audio/Video screens do not offer attachments.

title: Attaching files
heading: Supported formats
text:
| Category | Formats | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Documents | PDF, Word (.docx), Hangul (.hwp, .hwpx), PowerPoint (.pptx), Excel (.xlsx) | A scanned PDF is read page by page when the administrator has connected text from scans (OCR). |
| Text and code | .txt, .md, .csv, .tsv, .json, and most code files | Read as text. |
| Images | PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, TIFF, BMP | The text of a document photo is read with OCR. The picture itself goes only to **strict-local** models that support image recognition (marked 👁), as PNG, JPG, GIF or WebP of **4MB or smaller**. |
| Audio and video | mp3, wav, mp4, and similar | **25MB or smaller**. Converted to text and read when the administrator has connected speech transcription. |

The maximum size for a single file is 200MB. Older Office formats (.doc, .ppt, .xls) are not supported. A file that could not be read appears as **Unread attachment** in the processing steps of the answer.

title: Attaching files
heading: How long an attachment is referenced
text:
An attached file stays available to later requests in the same conversation. It appears in the processing steps as **Attachment from an earlier turn**.

- When a file is too large to process at once, only the **parts relevant to your question** are selected and sent. Ask something such as "Tell me what Article 7 says" and the text around that article is sent.
- If the answer is not in the part that was sent, the model searches inside the file with the **Find in files** tool.
- The processing steps mark each attachment as used, truncated, or omitted.

The Reports and Slides screens do not carry over attachments from earlier requests, so attach the material for the document to that request directly. Files attached in another conversation are not referenced on their own either. Attach a file you already uploaded again with **+** → **Choose from Files**, and to use the same material in many conversations all the time, register it in a project. Where the administrator has turned on **Internal material stays strict-local**, a request with attachments is answered by the strict-local twin of the same model. Privacy

title: Attaching files
heading: Files
text:
**Files** in the left menu holds every file of your account, under two tabs.

- **Uploaded**: files you attached to conversations or uploaded to projects
- **Made in conversations**: files made during a conversation, such as code-run outputs (CSV and the like), images and charts

Each row shows the size, when it came, and which conversation or project it belongs to. Find files by name, download them, and delete one or a selection. Deleting a project file takes it out of the project too.

To use the same material again in a new chat, report or deck, pick it under **+** → **Choose from Files** in the input box. Nothing is uploaded again, so there is no wait.

When you delete a conversation you can tick **Also delete the conversation's files**. Left unticked, its files stay in Files. Project files are never deleted with a conversation.

title: Attaching files
heading: Improving recognition accuracy
text:
- State exactly what you are looking for. "Summarize this file" is less accurate than "List only the remote work application steps from this file".
- Attach table-heavy material as Excel or CSV rather than PDF. It is read far more accurately that way.
- For an attached Hangul file (.hwpx), select **Open as document** on the file chip to convert it straight into an editable report. The conversion calls no model, so it uses no credits.

title: Attaching files
heading: Scanned PDFs and document photos
text:
When the administrator has connected text from scans (OCR), the text of PDF pages without a text layer and of document photos is read inside the organization after upload.

- The file chip and the project and agent material lists show progress, such as **Reading text, page 3 of 10**. Ask before it finishes and the answer draws only on the pages read so far, and says it cannot know the rest.
- The OCR engine reads first; pages it is unsure of, and pages with a table, are read again by a strict-local model that reads pictures. Page pictures go nowhere else.
- Where the two readings differ in words or numbers, the file shows **n pages to check**. Compare important values such as amounts and dates with the original.
- A photo with hardly any text is treated as a picture only.
- The administrator sets how many pages of one document are read. Past that, the file shows **first n pages**.

title: Attaching files
heading: Attaching images
text: Images are sent only to strict-local models that support image recognition. The personal data check reads text only, so images never go to a model that may send data outside the organization. If you select any other model, the file is attached but the model cannot see its content. Images from earlier requests are not sent again, so attach the image again to ask more about it.

title: Choosing a model
text: Select the model name to the right of the composer to open the list. When eight or more models are registered, a **Find a model** search box appears with it.

title: Choosing a model
heading: What the model list shows
text:
| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **strict-local** | The model is confirmed to run only on organization servers and to send nothing outside. Selecting it disables web search, page reading, and connectors. |
| **self-hosted · strict unverified** | The model runs on organization servers, but it is not confirmed that there is no external fallback path. |
| **May switch to an external provider** | The model normally runs on organization servers, but it may switch to an external service during an outage. |
| **External provider** | The model is supplied by an external service, so requests are sent outside the organization. |
| **Boundary unverified** | No information about the processing location is provided for this model. |
| Price | Input and output credits per 1,000 tokens, or **Free** |
| Context | How much can be processed at once |
| 👁 · 🔧 | Image recognition supported · Tool calling supported |

Depending on how the gateway registers models, one model name can appear as two entries that differ only in the data boundary label. Check the label before you select one.

When a **May switch to an external provider** model fails to answer and the gateway's fallback model answers instead, the answer carries an **Answered by external fallback** badge (**Answered by fallback model** when the fallback also runs on organization servers). Hover over the badge to see the model you asked for and the one that answered. The same event is recorded in the administrator's audit log as **Fallback model answered**.

title: Choosing a model
heading: Auto mode
text:
When the administrator enables it on the Chat screen, two modes appear at the top of the list. These modes apply to the conversation, not to a model.

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| Auto · Quality first | Only the requests judged complex switch to the higher model the administrator set. Everything else uses the model you selected. |
| Auto · Cost saving | Switches simple requests to a cheaper model. Everything else uses the model you selected. |

Auto does not apply to requests that use files, projects, agents, skills, or web search set to Always. Those requests use the model you selected. A badge above the composer then shows that Auto was not applied. Each answer also shows the reason for the decision and an estimate of the credits saved.

title: Choosing a model
heading: Scope of a model selection
text:
- **Selecting on the home screen** saves the model to your account as the **default model** for that screen, such as Chat, Reports, or Slides. It applies when you sign in from another device, and you can also change it in Settings → Preferences.
- **Selecting during a conversation** applies to that conversation only.
- An agent conversation uses the model set on the agent. An agent with no model of its own (**Default model**) follows that screen's default model.
- When the administrator limits which models an account may use, only the allowed models appear.

title: Working with skills and building agents
text: Jobs such as minutes, a bullet-style briefing (개조식 보고) or comparing options are done with **official skills**. Turn a skill on in a conversation and it does that job; for work you do often, combine a few skills into an agent of your own. There are no separate built-in agents.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: Official skills
text:
Skills the administrator shares with everyone. They show under **Official skills** in the composer's **+** → **Skills**; picking one adds it to your skills and turns it on.

| Skill | Screen | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Meeting minutes (회의록 작성) | Report | Keeps decisions, action items (task · owner · due date · source · note) and open items from a transcript, notes and follow-up mails. Writes in the **회의록** template. A meeting length, period or question the material does not give, and an action row nobody was given, go back for one fix; what remains is taken out or marked 「(확인 필요)」. |
| Bullet-style briefing (개조식 보고) | Report | Turns notes and mails into a one-page □ ○ - ㆍ briefing a superior can decide from. **개조식 보고서** template, one page by default. |
| Compare-and-decide report (비교·결정 보고) | Report | Weighs 2–5 options on exactly the criteria asked and recommends one. **비교·분석 보고서** template. |
| Official document draft (공문·기안 초안) | Report | Drafts plans, result reports, approval drafts and notices. No web search; pictures only when asked. |
| Presentation deck (발표 자료 구성) | Slides | One claim per slide, the conclusion first. |
| Extract and tally (자료 추출·집계) | Chat | Reads Excel and CSV with code, pulls columns, totals by item into tables and charts, and records the rows it removed or changed. |
| Answers from regulations (규정 근거 답변) | Chat | Answers from regulations and guidelines with the article cited as [n], and points what the material does not cover to the department. |
| YouTube transcript and summary (YouTube 영상 전사·요약) | Chat | Gets the captions (or a transcription of the audio) through the **YouTube 전사** connector and summarises from that alone. |
| Deep research (심층 조사) | Chat | Searches the web and papers many times through the **심층 리서치** connector and sum

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: Other skills, and what a skill brings
text:
There are also Date calculation (with the **시간** (time) connector it reads today's date from there), Quote calculation, Excel cleanup, PDF table → Excel, Grounding check, Ask for missing information, Calculation and unit check and Mask personal information.

A skill brings its template, checks and missing-information questions. Turn on **Meeting minutes** on the report screen, for instance, and the template becomes **회의록** (if you picked another template, it writes in that one), it asks for the meeting date and attendees before writing, and checks sources and format afterwards. A skill you turn on stays on for the rest of the conversation, approving the outline included.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: Using a skill in a conversation
text:
1. Choose **Report** on the home screen.
2. In the composer choose **+** → **Skills** → **회의록 작성**. The template chip shows **회의록**.
3. Paste the meeting notes or transcript and send 「정식 회의록으로 만들어 줘」.

Skills turned on in chat also go along when you ask for a document there and it moves to a report or deck. Skills that need tools cannot run on that screen and are left out, with a notice naming them.

Use **개조식 보고** (「과장님께 올릴 1쪽 보고로」) and **비교·결정 보고** (「세 제품을 연간 비용과 필수 조건으로 비교해서 하나 골라 줘」) the same way.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: Translation, press releases, Excel files and charts
text:
- **번역** (Translation): turn it on in a conversation, paste the text and send something like 「영어로, 의역, 격식체로」 (into English, free, formal). To fix terms, add them: 「용어: 학생지원팀 = Student Support Office」. To translate a whole document as a document, turn it on on the report screen; it follows the source's headings and order and adds no summary or recommendation.
- **보도자료** (Press release): paste the event, agreement or award material and send 「보도자료로, A4 1장」. If the material has no quote, it writes no quote paragraph and says so at the end. When only a spokesperson's name is given (a CEO, say), it drafts one quote for that person from the material's purpose and plan and marks it 「(가안, 본인 확인 필요)」. On the report screen, say 「보도자료」 in the request and the page head gets the release date, embargo and contact fields.
- **엑셀 파일 만들기** (Make an Excel file): paste a table or attach a CSV or Excel file and send 「엑셀 파일로, 합계 행과 증감률 열은 수식으로」 (as an Excel file, total row and change-rate column as formulas). The file appears under the answer as a download button. For a messy sheet, turn on **엑셀 정리** (Excel cleanup) too; for aggregates, **자료 추출·집계** (Extract and tally), and you get the computed table as a file. Code execution (the sandbox) must be on.
