- **차트 만들기** (Make a chart): paste a table and send 「지점별 월 매출을 막대 차트로」 (monthly sales by branch as a bar chart); the chart opens beside the conversation. To put the chart inside the Excel file too, turn on **엑셀 파일 만들기** as well and add 「엑셀 차트도」.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: Before the meeting: the agenda
text: The **회의 안건** (Meeting agenda) template is the minutes' counterpart. On the report screen choose **+** → template picker → **회의 안건** (or say 「회의 안건」 or 「안건지」 in the request) and send the items and their owners. It writes the same head as the minutes (meeting, date and time, place, attendees, author), an agenda table (order · item · owner · time · goal), points to review per item, pre-reads and the decisions needed. The goal is one of 보고 (information), 논의 (discussion) or 결정 (decision); an owner the material does not name is 「미정」 with one line saying what to confirm. Without a meeting date or attendees in the material, it asks before writing.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: Building an agent from skills
text: In **Customize** → **Agents** → **Add** → **Create an agent**, the skills you choose under **Skills and tools** › **Skills kept on** are on in every conversation with that agent (up to six). The list shows your skills and the **official skills** you have not added yet; picking one adds it to your skills. Picking a skill that works only on reports or slides sets the agent's first screen to that screen. Each skill's template, checks and missing-information questions come with it; a template or detailed settings set on the agent itself come first. **Skills you can pick in the composer** narrows what can be turned on during a conversation.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: A minutes agent
text:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | Our team's minutes |
| Instructions | 작성자는 「기획팀 [이름]」으로 적는다. 실행 항목은 담당 팀 순서로 정렬한다. (Only your team's specifics; the skill knows how to write minutes) |
| Skills kept on | 회의록 작성 |
| Extra work | Prepare before writing · Review after writing · Finish (export a file when done: HWPX) |
| Template & theme › Theme | 문서용 명조 |
| Advanced › Screens | Report |

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: A briefing agent
text: Skills kept on **개조식 보고**, theme **문서용 명조**, screen **Report**. Put only what never changes in the instructions, such as the addressee (「시설과장님」) and the approval line.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: A purchase review agent
text: Skills kept on **비교·결정 보고** + **견적 계산**, screen **Report**. Write your organization's criteria in the instructions (「판단 기준은 3년 총비용, 유지보수, 도입 일정 순서」) so no request has to repeat them.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: A tally agent
text: Skills kept on **자료 추출·집계**; under Skills and tools › Tools, **파일 작업**, **차트 그리기** and **수치 계산**; screen **Chat**. Upload a spreadsheet and ask 「부서별 합계와 비율을 표로」; it first asks for the deadline, period or denominator basis when the material does not give it.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: A regulations chatbot
text:
1. Create an agent with **규정 근거 답변** + **날짜 계산** kept on.
2. Upload the regulation files under **Sources** and fill in **Department and contact**.
3. Under **Extra work**, tick **공개 전 점검** (the pre-publication check: hold answers without grounds · point to the department · mask personal information).
4. Try it, then publish it as a chatbot. The bot answers with the skills' instructions frozen into the published version.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: Video and research agents
text:
- **Lecture video notes**: **YouTube 영상 전사·요약** kept on, screen **Chat**. Write the shape you want in the instructions (「핵심 다섯 줄과 용어 풀이 표」). The **YouTube 전사** connector must be on.
- **Trend research**: **심층 조사** + **근거 대조** kept on, screen **Chat**. The **심층 리서치** connector must be on, and one run takes a few minutes.

title: Working with skills and building agents
heading: Making the same as your own skill
text: You can make a skill like the official ones yourself. In **Customize** → **Skills** → **Add**, write the steps, and under **Server checks** choose **Template to write in**, **Checks it brings**, the strictness, **Web search** and **Pictures**, and **Missing-information questions**. In an uploaded SKILL.md, put `template`, `checks`, `check_options`, `questions` and `process` in the front matter.

title: Templates and themes
text:
A template is the structure of an artifact; a theme is its look. Work you do often belongs to agents. Neither is a Customize tab: you pick each where it is used.

| Feature | Role | Where to pick it | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Template** | The structure of the artifact (structure rules, typesetting, check items). There are built-in templates and your own. | **+** → **Pick a template** in the composer; **Template & theme** › **Template** in the agent settings | That conversation (clear it with × on the chip), or the conversations that agent opens |
| **Theme** | A setting that bundles colors, typefaces, and writing style. | **Template & theme** › **Theme** in the agent settings, **Edit › Theme** in the report or slides panel, the project settings | That agent's or project's artifacts |

title: Templates and themes
heading: Templates
text:
A template defines the structure rules and the typesetting of reports and slides. Select one and the **What this template checks** list appears. You edit a document in a template by rewriting it one block at a time, and you can export it as PDF, DOCX/PPTX, HWPX, HTML, or text. Create your own document template with **New template** in the template picker or the agent settings (Agents and skills). Images, audio and video have no templates.

The built-in templates in the picker are seven documents (**Internal approval draft (간이기안문)**, **Implementation plan (draft)**, **Results report**, **Bullet-style briefing (개조식)**, **Comparison report**, **Meeting minutes**, **Meeting agenda**) and the **Briefing deck**. They write straight into the organization's format and show that format's check results when done. Conversations and agents that use a hidden template keep writing and exporting with it.

title: Templates and themes
heading: Themes
text:
Manage them in **Settings** → **Themes** (also opened by **Manage themes** in the agent settings). Themes other people shared appear under **Shared themes** on the same tab.

- Set the name, the accent color, the body color, the secondary color, the typeface (sans-serif or serif), the writing style rules, the image style, and the rules to apply alongside them.
- **Import from a document** extracts a draft from an existing hwpx, docx, or pdf file, or from a web address. It calls the model once, and you can review the content before saving.
- The writing style applies to conversations, reports, and slides. Colors and typefaces apply to slides and report covers. The image style applies to images. Nothing applies to audio and video.
- Theme settings are copied into an artifact when it is generated. Changing the theme later does not change artifacts that already exist.
- An administrator can distribute a read-only shared theme with **Provide to all users**.
- Of the built-in themes, the pickers show **Default** (기본) and **Document serif** (문서용 명조).

title: Web search and tools
text:
Choose **Web search** from the **+** button in the composer and set it to **Auto**, **Always** or **Off**. Auto is the default; Always or Off shows as a chip in the composer. The setting applies to that request only, and it resets to **Auto** in a new conversation.

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| Auto | Searches first when you ask about information that changes over time, such as news, prices, schedules, latest versions, and weather, or that must be exact: phone numbers and hotlines, laws, tax rates, thresholds and benefits, fees, rates and limits, event dates, whether a product or service is available, organizations, and statistics. Legal, tax, financial and health advice is searched first too. Otherwise it searches only when the model judges it necessary. |
| Always | Always performs a search for that request. |
| Off | Does not search unless you ask explicitly, with wording such as "search for" or "look it up". |

When a search runs, the answer shows numbers in the form `[n]` and a source list. One request performs at most three searches and reads at most six pages. Weather uses a dedicated tool instead of search. If you select a strict-local model, web search cannot be chosen.

Writing, translation and proofreading, code and spreadsheet formulas, role-play, concept explanations, and questions about attached or pasted material are not searched first in Auto. A draft, edit, translation or code fix made from what you give (a meeting agenda, an email draft, a bug in pasted code) is not searched at all in Auto unless it names something to look up, such as "latest", an exchange rate or the weather (choose **Always** to search anyway). A follow-up (for example "it's 30 million won I need within a year" after an investment question) is judged with the conversation befo

title: Web search and tools
heading: Grounding check for legal, tax, financial and health questions
text: Legal, tax, financial and health advice gets the **grounding check** by default. An amount, rate or threshold, a phone number or hotline, a dose, or a legal consequence such as a criminal penalty or a fine that is not in this turn's search results or in what you gave is marked **(확인 필요)** ("needs checking") where it stands. When there are many marks, they come out of the text and are listed once at the end of the answer. Practical guidance (what to do, which documents to prepare, when to see a professional) stays as written. The result appears in the processing steps as an item such as **근거 확인(법률)** ("grounding check (legal)").

title: Web search and tools
heading: Tools the model uses
text:
Models that support tool calling, marked 🔧 in the list, use the following tools as the request requires. Their use appears in the processing steps.

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| Web search · Page reading · Weather | Runs searches and reads the body text of the pages it needs. |
| Code execution | Performs calculations, table processing, and chart generation with real code. This path is accurate for arithmetic on large numbers. |
| Arithmetic check | Calculates arithmetic and powers exactly on the server, and compares the result with answer choices or a submitted answer. It needs no extra server, and requests that call for a calculation use it first. |
| Find in files | Searches inside attached files and agent material. |
| Artifacts · Chart creation | Produces an artifact: a document or a chart in the right panel. |
| Shared notes | Leaves a note for other conversations in the same project to reference. |
| Connectors | External tools that you installed. Connectors |

Where the administrator has not connected a search server or a code execution server, those tools are not available.

title: Frequently asked questions
text:
This page lists causes and actions by symptom. To look something up by the error message shown on the screen, see Limits and troubleshooting.

### I signed up but I cannot sign in
Your account is waiting for approval. The waiting screen switches over automatically once an administrator approves it. Use **Contact the administrator** on the waiting screen to get in touch.

### I typed in Chat but it switched to the report screen
A sentence that asks for a document, such as "Write a report" or "Make a slide deck", switches automatically to a new conversation on that screen. The document is written with that screen's default model; when it differs from the model picked in Chat, a note above the input box says so. Short pieces such as a press release, notice or email stay in Chat and are written there (to get one as a report, ask on the report screen). To continue in Chat, phrase the request around existing content, such as "Summarize this".

### It says the file I attached could not be read
The file is an older Office format (.doc, .ppt, .xls), or a scan while text from scans (OCR) is not connected. Attach it again as a PDF, Word, Hangul, Excel, or text file that contains text, or ask the administrator to connect text from scans. Attaching files

### My next question does not refer to the file I attached
The attachment stays available throughout the same Chat conversation. Check whether the processing steps of the answer show "Attachment from an earlier turn". Other conversations and the report and slide screens do not carry earlier attachments over. If the file is long, only the parts related to your question are passed, so describe what you are looking for in detail.

### The answer does not match the facts
The model may have generated something it does not know. Set web

title: Glossary
text:
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Screen (Chat · Report · Slides · Image · Audio/Video) | The screen you choose on the home page. Administrators turn each one on and off |
| Conversation (대화) | The record of one piece of work. One row in the sidebar |
| Artifact (아티팩트) | A document, deck, chart or other file produced in a conversation. The right-hand panel and the gallery |
| Template (템플릿) | The structure of the artifact (structure rules, typesetting, check items). It stays for the whole conversation |
| Theme (테마) | The look of the artifact (colors, typefaces, tone). Attached to an agent or a project, kept in Settings › Themes |
| Project (프로젝트) | A workspace that groups material, instructions, and conversations |
| Agent (에이전트) | A helper with set instructions, process, tools, and material. Start one from **+** → **Agents** in the composer |
| How it works (진행 과정) | The order an agent works in: Answer directly · Start from a base process · Set it up yourself (advanced) |
| Base process (기본 과정) | The working order of a built-in agent (Bullet-style briefing, Minutes, …). Used only by agents that already started from it |
| Bundle (묶음) | A group of things an agent does before and after writing. Ticked under Extra work in the agent settings |
| Skill (스킬) | A way of working you keep on in a conversation. Up to 3 in the composer, up to 6 as an agent's skills kept on. Brings its template, checks and missing-information questions |
| Official skill (공식 스킬) | A skill the administrator shares with everyone, for jobs such as minutes or a bullet-style briefing. Picking it in the composer adds it to your skills |
| Hidden (숨김) | A built-in skill, template, theme or connector kept but not shown in the lists, the store or the pickers. It still works in bundles and earlier conversatio

title: KloudChat User Guide
text: KloudChat is an AI assistant your organization runs on its own servers. It answers questions, reads the documents you attach, and writes reports and slide decks. To see where the model that generates an answer runs, check the **data boundary** label in the model list.

title: KloudChat User Guide
heading: Guide pages by purpose
text:
| Purpose | Feature used | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Questions and answers, code review, proofreading | Home → **Chat** | Conversation basics |
| Getting answers grounded in a document you attach | **+** → **Attach files or photos** in the composer | Attaching files |
| Getting answers based on up-to-date information | **+** → Web search in the composer | Web search and tools |
| Writing a report | Home → **Report** | Writing reports |
| Writing a slide deck | Home → **Slides** | Writing slides |
| Editing a finished document yourself and having it reviewed | The ribbon in the artifact panel | Artifact editor |
| Generating images, audio and video | Home → **Image**, **Audio/Video** | Images and audio/video |
| Passing an artifact on as a link | **Share** at the top of the conversation | Sharing |
| Grouping files and instructions for repeated use | Sidebar → **Projects** | Projects |
| Delegating to an assistant with a defined role | **+** → Agents in the composer | Agents and skills |
| Opening an agent to others as a chatbot | Agent page → **Publish as a chatbot** | Publishing a chatbot |
| Getting an artifact in a set template | **+** → **Pick a template** in the composer | Templates and themes |
| Storing information you have to repeat often | Account menu → **Settings** → **Memory** | Memory |
| Calling models from external tools and code | Account menu → **API access** | API and coding tool integration |
| Checking usage and tidying up conversations | Account menu → **Usage**, **Conversation history** | Usage and conversation history |
| Reporting a bug or requesting a feature | Account menu → **Feedback & issues** | Feedback and issues |

title: KloudChat User Guide
heading: Reading order
text:
If you are new to the product, read Signing up and signing in, Home screen layout and Conversation basics in that order. If something goes wrong, Limits and troubleshooting helps you trace the cause from the message shown on screen. Terms you have not seen before are collected in Glossary.

This guide covers the full feature set of the product. The following items depend on your organization's settings, so check with your administrator if the screen differs from this guide.

- **Available screens**: Chat is always provided. Report, Slides, Image and Audio/Video appear only when the administrator enables them.
- **Model list and charging**: The models on offer, their names, data boundaries and credit rates differ between organizations.
- **Sign-up method and email domains**: The administrator sets the approval procedure and the permitted domains.
- **Integrated features**: Web search, code execution, dictation, file search and text reading (OCR) work only when the administrator has connected a server.
- **Service name and logo**: The administrator can change these, so the names on screen may differ from this guide.

title: Limits and troubleshooting
text: This page describes the limits the service allows and what to do for each error message shown on the screen.

title: Limits and troubleshooting
heading: Limits
text:
| Item | Limit |
|---|---|
| A single file | 200MB |
| Images | PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, up to 4MB, on a strict-local model that supports image recognition |
| Audio and video files | 25MB, when speech transcription is connected |
| Number of slides | Up to 50 slides (5 to 12 if you do not specify a number) |
| Number of report sections | 3 to 12 sections |
| Skills | 3 per request |
| Memory | Up to 40 entries passed per request |
| Opening sentences (agent) | 6 |
| API keys | 10 per account |
| Slide image upload | 5MB |
| Amount of file content in one conversation | About 35% of the model window (up to about 150,000 characters). Beyond that, only the relevant parts |
| Answer length | No upper limit. Stops automatically when the text starts repeating |

title: Limits and troubleshooting
heading: Processing time limits
text:
- A single request runs for up to 15 minutes. Past that it ends with an error.
- If the model sends nothing for 3 minutes, the request ends with an error. In that case use **Another model**.
- Reports and slide decks are written in order, section by section or slide by slide. A 20-slide deck takes several minutes, and video generation takes longer and shows progress.

title: Limits and troubleshooting
heading: What to do for each error message
text:
Search for the message exactly as it appears on the screen.

| Message on the screen | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| You have used all of your credits this month | The monthly limit is used up | Wait for the refill on the 1st of next month. Free models are not affected |
| You do not have enough credits this month | The remaining credits are less than the estimated cost of this request | Reduce the options such as length or resolution, or use a free model |
| Cannot connect to the model server | Model gateway failure | Try again shortly. Contact your administrator if it continues |
| Could not get an answer because of a model server error | The gateway refused the request (including when the files or the conversation exceed the model window) | Upload the files again in a new conversation, or narrow the question |
| The model did not respond, so the request was stopped. Try generating again with another model | No text arrived for 3 minutes | **Another model** |
| The model server request limit was exceeded | Gateway rate limit | Try again shortly |
| The model server refused authentication | Gateway key problem | Contact your administrator |
| The model server does not have this model | The model list has changed | Choose another model. The administrator refreshes the list |
| This model is not allowed for this account | A model the administrator has restricted | Choose another model |
| This model cannot be used on this screen right now | The screen (a report, for example) and the model do not match | Change the model |
| No models are available right now | The gateway is not connected | Contact your administrator |
| The request was not sent because the personal data checker is unavailable | Protection feature failure | Contact your administrator. Sending is

title: Limits and troubleshooting
heading: Features that are not provided
text:
- Editing a sent message inside the same conversation. **Edit message** creates a new conversation with the edited message. Conversation basics
- Several users editing one conversation together. Sharing is read only.
- Two-factor authentication.
- Keyboard shortcuts on the mobile screen. The tools are in the bottom sheet that opens from the **+** button in the composer.

title: Limits and troubleshooting
heading: Model limitations
text: A model can present things it does not know as if they were fact. For information that changes or cannot be memorized, such as organization details, dates, and figures, turn on web search or attach source material. An answer that shows no sources is an answer that did not go through search. You can check a report against its sources with **Fact check**, and calculations are verified with **Arithmetic check** or **Code execution**.

title: Feedback and issues
text: Report an error, request a feature or ask the administrators a question. Account menu → **Feedback & issues** lists what you sent, its status and the administrators' replies.

title: Feedback and issues
heading: Sending
text:
- On the **Feedback & issues** page, select **New report** (bug report) or **New question**. The type is one of **Bug report**, **Feature request** and **Question**.
- After you press 👎 on an answer, a **Report** button appears beside it. It opens the form with that answer and the artifact it made filled in as the **Pinned item**.
- You can add one screenshot (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, 5 MB or smaller).

title: Feedback and issues
heading: What is sent with it
text:
- Always sent: app build, browser, screen size, language. When sent from a conversation, also the conversation type, the model used, the agent and process, stage status and failure reasons, and artifact version numbers.
- Only when you tick **Share this session with the administrators** are the conversation, the versions of the artifacts it made, the stage records and its files copied as they are at that moment. Later edits or deletion of the conversation do not change the copy.
- A conversation that ran on the internal-material route (strict-local) needs **I know this contains internal material and share it** ticked before the copy can be sent.

title: Feedback and issues
heading: Status
text: The status moves through **Received · Checking · Resolved · On hold**. When an administrator replies, **Feedback & issues** in the account menu shows the number of **New reply** items. An administrator opening the session copy is recorded in the audit log.

title: Memory
text: Memory holds information to be used across conversations, not just one. It stores your affiliation, tasks in progress, notation rules, and similar details.

title: Memory
heading: How to save
text:
- **Automatic saving**: Turn on **Save memory automatically** under Settings → Preferences. Each time an answer ends, the system selects and saves content that stays valid. The default is off, and content already saved is not saved twice. When something is saved, "n memories saved" appears at the bottom of the answer.
- **Adding directly**: Enter it in **Settings** → **Memory** → New memory.
- **Project memory**: Manage it in the Memory tab of the project detail screen. Conclusions that an agent leaves through Share note are also saved there.

title: Memory
heading: Fields
text:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Use lowercase English letters and hyphens. Other memories can reference it in the form `[[name]]`. |
| Type | Choose from user, feedback, project, and reference. |
| Description | Describe in one line when it should be referenced. |
| Scope | Set it to global (all conversations) or to a single project. |
| Pinned | A pinned memory is delivered first to every conversation. |

title: Memory
heading: How memory is delivered
text:
Each request delivers up to 40 items, based on pinned items and recent items. The processing steps of the answer show "n memories referenced". Beyond 40 items the oldest ones are excluded, so delete memories you do not use.

Information saved incorrectly can be edited on the Memory screen. If **About me** in Settings and the content of memory differ, answers can become inconsistent, so keep them aligned. Memory is not included in share links.

title: Projects
text: A project is a workspace that binds materials, instructions, and conversations together. Use it to reference the same materials from several conversations, or to avoid entering common rules every time.

title: Projects
heading: Creating
text: Go to the sidebar → **Projects** → New project, then enter a name, a description, and **project instructions**. After creation, the detail screen lets you set the icon, the theme, and the **default template** for each screen (reports, slide decks).

title: Projects
heading: Tabs
text:
| Tab | Function |
|---|---|
| Conversations | Start a new conversation in this project, and add existing conversations to the project or remove them from it. |
| Knowledge | Add files and register addresses as **web material**. Web material stores the content as it was at registration time. It shows how many tokens each file uses and how much of the context it takes up. You can check the recognized content, download the original, and delete it. |
| Skills | Skills you pick with **Choose skills** appear first in this project's composer. |
| Memory | Memory shared at the project level. Conclusions that an agent leaves through **Share note** also accumulate here. |

title: Projects
heading: How knowledge is delivered
text: Project knowledge is delivered automatically to every conversation in the project. If the volume fits within the processing range, all of it is delivered. If it exceeds the range, only the parts related to the question are selected and delivered. If even the selected volume exceeds the range, only the file list is delivered. The processing steps of the answer show how much of it was used. In reports it is cited with source numbers.

title: Projects
heading: Instructions
text: Describe rules that apply to every conversation, such as "answer in polite language" or "give English terms alongside". They take precedence over personalization settings.

title: Projects
heading: Deleting a project
text: Deleting a project deletes its instructions and knowledge files. Conversations are detached from the project and kept, and artifacts and memory also remain.

title: Projects
heading: Comparison with conversation attachments
text:
| Item | Conversation attachment | Project knowledge |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | That conversation | Every conversation in the project |
| Retention | Until the conversation is deleted | Until the file is deleted |
| Share link | Exposed only to the extent that the answer quotes it | Not exposed |

title: Settings
text: **Settings**, in the account menu, has seven tabs: Profile, Preferences, Personalization, Memory, Themes, API keys and Security.

title: Settings
heading: Profile
text: You can change your name (the password is on the **Security** tab). You can check your role and join date, the remaining credits and the allowance for this month, and the next refill date. Credits are reset to the allowance on the first day of each month and do not carry over. The email address cannot be changed.

title: Settings
heading: Preferences
text:
| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Default model per screen | The model applied to new conversations on each screen, such as Chat, Reports, and Slides. It is saved to the account, so it applies the same way on every device. |
| A request with personal data in it → What to do by default | Choose from asking every time, switching to strict-local, masking, and sending the original text (when the administrator allows it). Privacy |
| A request with personal data in it → strict-local picture model | The model that draws a picture in a conversation or document with internal material when it must stay strict-local and the picked picture model is external. Shown only when there is more than one strict-local picture model. Unset, `strict-local/z-image-turbo` is used, or the first in the list when that model is not served. |
| Response streaming | When it is off, the answer is shown all at once after it is complete. |
| Save memory automatically | Automatically saves information that stays valid, for each answer. |
| Hold Space to dictate | Hold `Space` in an empty composer and speak; on release the words are typed into the box, not sent. Shown only when speech transcription is connected, and off by default. |
| Token and credit display | Sets whether usage is shown at the bottom of the answer. |

The theme and the language are switched with the buttons at the top right of the screen, not in this tab.

title: Settings
heading: Text size
text: KloudChat has no text-size setting of its own. To read larger text, zoom the browser: `Ctrl` + `+` on Windows (`Ctrl` + `-` to shrink, `Ctrl` + `0` to reset), `Cmd` + `+` on a Mac. At 200% the screen reflows and stays usable. On a phone, pinch to zoom.

title: Settings
heading: Personalization
text:
- **Things worth knowing about me**: Describe your affiliation, your area of work, your level of understanding, and similar details. It applies **to conversations only** and is not delivered to reports or slide decks.
- **Answer style**: Describe the length, the tone, and the format. It applies to both conversations and documents. Write entries such as "no introduction", "always include an example", or "give English terms alongside".

The settings apply from the next conversation onward. If an agent or a project has instructions, those take precedence. You can open the tab directly with `Alt+Shift+P`, and when it is applied the processing steps of the answer show **Personalization applied**.

title: Settings
heading: Memory
text: See and edit what is remembered across conversations. See Memory for details.

title: Settings
heading: Themes
text: A theme is a document's or deck's colours, typeface and writing rules. Make and edit them under **My themes**; **Import from a document** reads a draft from an existing hwpx, docx or pdf. **Shared themes** lists the ones others shared. You pick a theme under **Template & theme** › **Theme** in the agent settings (**Manage themes** beside it opens this tab) and in the report or slides panel's **Edit › Theme**. Templates and themes

title: Settings
heading: API keys
text: Issue keys for use in external tools or scripts. You can issue up to 10 keys per account. The key value is shown only once at issue time, so copy it immediately. In the list you can check the issue date and the last use time. **Revoke** blocks a key immediately. The allowed model limits set on the account apply to keys in the same way. Integrating the API and coding tools

title: Settings
heading: Security
text:
- **Signed-in devices**: Shows the browser, the IP, and the last use time. The current device is marked, and individual sign-out and **Sign out all other devices** are provided. Calls made through an API key are not shown in this list.
- **Change password**: Enter the current password and a new password of at least 10 characters. Changing it signs out the sessions on your other devices.
- **Sign-in history**: Shows the last 100 sign-ins, failed sign-ins, password changes, and keys issued, together with the IP, the region, and the browser. Region information is shown only when the administrator has configured location data, and private networks are marked as "internal network".
- Two-factor authentication is not provided. Use a sufficiently long password and sign out the devices you do not recognize.

title: Usage and conversation history
text: Check your credit usage and tidy up past conversations.

title: Usage and conversation history
heading: Usage
text:
Check it in the account menu → **Usage**.

- It provides the remaining credits and the allowance for this month, a period selector, and a daily trend of credits or answer counts.
- It shows usage separately **by model**, **by screen** (Chat, Reports, Slides, Images, API keys, and so on), and **by API key**. Requests sent with an API key are added to this month's credits and to each breakdown within a few minutes, and share the same monthly limit.
- Voice transcription is shown separately in seconds and material indexing in chunks.

title: Usage and conversation history
heading: Credits
text:
A credit is the unit that expresses model usage, and the basis differs by type.

| Type | Billing unit |
|---|---|
| Text | Per 1,000 tokens. Input and output are counted separately. |
| Image | Per image |
| Audio | Per call |
| Video | Per second × the combination of resolution and sound. Charged only when the generation completes. |

Models marked **Free** do not consume credits. Most of them are models the organization runs itself, but models that an external service offers free of charge are marked the same way. In that case the request is sent outside the organization. Check the data boundary label in the model list as well.

Credits are reset to the allowance on the first day of each month and do not carry over. When they are used up, you cannot send new requests until the next refill, but artifacts already created are kept. A request whose generation was stopped is recorded as an estimate.

title: Usage and conversation history
heading: Conversation history
text:
Check it in the account menu → **Conversation history**.

- View all conversations by date and search them by title and message text.
- You can use **Select all** on the listed items and then **Delete selected**, or run **Delete all conversations**. A confirmation dialog is shown before it runs.
- Deleting a conversation also deletes the artifacts created in that conversation and its share links. Projects and memory are kept.
- Where the administrator has set a retention period, the body of a conversation past that period is deleted automatically. Sign-in history and usage totals are kept.

title: Privacy
text: This page explains where your input and attachments are stored, how far they are sent, and how detected personal data is handled.

title: Privacy
heading: Where data is stored and sent
text:
| Data | Storage location | Sent outside | Deletion point | Administrator access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Conversations and answers | Organization server | Follows the data boundary of the model. Requests to models marked **external provider** and **may switch to an external provider** are sent to that service; requests to **strict-local** models are not. | When the user deletes it, or when the retention period set by the administrator has passed | No viewing screen. Exceptions: a session copy the user attached to Feedback and issues, and an abuse check of a published chatbot's conversations (recorded with its reason in the audit log). |
| Attachments and project knowledge | Organization server | Same as conversations. | When the file, the conversation, or the project is deleted | Only the storage volume can be checked. |
| Memory | Organization server | Sent to the model together with the request. | When the user deletes it | Cannot be viewed. |
| Web search terms | Not stored. | Sent to the search engine when search mode is Always or Auto. | Not applicable | Cannot be viewed. |
| Image and video prompts | Organization server | Follows the data boundary of the selected model, and in most cases is sent to an external service. | When the artifact is deleted | Cannot be viewed. |
| Usage and sign-in history | Organization server | Not sent. | Follows the policy set by the administrator. | Can be viewed. It includes tokens, credits, sign-ins, and policy application records. The values of detected personal data are not recorded; only the type and the count are kept. |

The **data boundary**, which differs by model, is shown in the model list. Choosing a model

title: Privacy
heading: Personal data detection
text:
KloudChat detects phone numbers, national ID numbers, payment card numbers, IP addresses, private keys, API keys and JWT tokens, and email addresses. Names and addresses are excluded from detection.

### Chat

If the administrator has enabled **Personal data protection for external models** and the selected model may send data outside, the **"This request contains personal data"** dialog appears before the request is sent. It states the detected types and counts, and does not show the values themselves.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Switch to a safe local model | Sends this request to the strict-local model designated by the administrator. |
| Mask and keep the current model | Replaces the personal data with placeholders before sending. |
| Send the original text to the external model | Sends the original text as it is. Shown only when the administrator allows it. |
| Return to editing | Returns to the input box without sending. |

To avoid choosing every time, set the default action in **A request with personal data in it** → **What to do by default** under Settings → Preferences.

### Reports, slide decks, images, and the API

When you write a report or a slide deck, generate an image, or call the API, detected personal data is masked and sent without a confirmation step.

### When always-on masking is set

Personal data is masked in every request, and **the conversation history is also stored in masked form**. When you open it again later, only the placeholders are shown, and sending the original text is not allowed. "Stored masked in the history" appears at the bottom of the answer.

title: Privacy
heading: Internal material stays strict-local
text:
When the administrator turns on this policy, a request that carries attachments, project files or memory is answered by the strict-local twin of the chosen model instead, and that conversation never moves to an external model afterwards. Without a twin, the strict-local safe model set by the administrator answers. Without that either, the request is refused.

Pictures, charts and figures follow the same rule. In a project conversation, a conversation that had attachments, or a strict-local conversation, they are made only on a strict-local model whatever model was picked, and are not made when no strict-local model is available. When the picked picture model is external, the **strict-local picture model** in Settings → Preferences draws it.

Document edits (rewriting a section, slide or block, a review, reading a theme from a file) follow the same rule. A document made in such a conversation is edited only on a strict-local model, and so is a document holding personal data: it is not masked, because masking would leave placeholders in the document. When no strict-local model is available, the edit is not made. A web fact-check sends the claims to outside search engines, so it is not run on such a document.

title: Privacy
heading: strict-local models
text: These are models confirmed not to send anything outside. Selecting one disables web search, page reading, and connectors. A model whose name starts with `local/` runs on the organization's servers first but may fall back to an external model, so it is not strict-local. Check the label in the list.

title: Privacy
heading: Share links
text: A shared conversation can be viewed by all signed-in users or by anyone who knows the link, depending on the scope you set. Sharing

title: Home screen layout
text: Signing in opens the home screen. Use the sidebar on the left to find past conversations, and the middle area to start new work.

title: Home screen layout
heading: Sidebar
text:
| Area | Description |
|---|---|
| Search | Searches past conversations (titles and messages) and artifacts. Shortcut `Ctrl+K`. |
| New chat | Goes to the home screen so you can start new work. Shortcut `Alt+Shift+N`. |
| Projects · Artifacts · Files · Customize | Goes to the workspace that holds your grouped files, the gallery of generated artifacts, the files you uploaded or made, and the place to manage agents (including ones others shared), skills and connectors. |
| Conversation list | Shown in the order **Pinned**, **Recent**. **All conversations** opens the history page. Icons show the type of each item. The `…` menu on an item lets you rename it, pin it, remove it from a project and delete it. |
| Credit this month | The usage you have left. Press it to go to the usage screen. A model marked **Free** does not consume credit. |
| Account menu | Customize, History, Agent setup, API access, Usage, Settings (including memory and themes), Feedback & issues, Keyboard shortcuts, the Manage menu (administrators), Sign out. |

title: Home screen layout
heading: Choosing a screen and using the composer
text:
Choose the screen you want from **Chat · Report · Slides** and type your request. If the administrator has enabled them, you can also choose **Image** and **Audio/Video**. Chat is for questions and answers. Report and Slides confirm the structure first and then write the document.

If you ask for a document in Chat, for example "Write a report" or "Make a slide deck", **the request moves automatically to a new conversation for that task.** Agent conversations and requests about existing content such as "Summarize this" or "Review this" stay in Chat.

| Feature | Description | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| **+** | One menu holding Attach files or photos, Pick a template, Skills, Web search, Connectors and Agents. On a phone it opens as a bottom sheet. | — |
| Attach files or photos | Uploads a file. You can drag and drop files or paste them. Pasting long text turns it into a **Pasted text** chip. | The whole conversation |
| 🎤 Dictate | Turns speech into text. Shown only when the administrator has connected speech transcription. | That input |
| Pick a template | Selects the template for reports and slides. Not offered in Chat, Image or Audio/Video. | That conversation |
| Skills | Selects up to three skills to apply to the request. | That request |
| Web search: Auto · Always · Off | Chooses the web search mode. **Always** or **Off** shows as a chip in the composer. | That request. A new conversation resets it automatically |
| Connectors | Turns the connectors you have installed on and off. | Your whole account |
| Agents | Selects an agent and starts a new conversation with that agent. | — |
| Model name ▾ | Selects the model to use. | Choosing it on Home makes it your account default, while choosing it during a conversation applies it to that conversation |
| ↑ · ■ |

title: Home screen layout
heading: Example requests and work in progress
text:
- **Example requests**: Examples suited to the chosen screen (Chat, Report, Slides and so on) are shown. Selecting one fills the composer; it does not send. Pick an agent from **+** → **Agents** in the composer. Agents and skills
- **In progress**: Shown while a long task such as video generation is running.

title: Home screen layout
heading: Buttons at the top right
text: There are **Share** (on the conversation screen), **Install app** (installs a shortcut app in browsers that support it), **EN** (language switch) and a theme button. The theme cycles through system, light and dark.

title: Home screen layout
heading: Mobile screen
text: Press **+** in the composer to open Attach files or photos, Pick a template, Skills, Web search, Connectors and Agents in a bottom sheet. The processing details of an answer are collapsed as "n processing details".

title: Keyboard shortcuts
text: Press `Ctrl+/` anywhere on the screen to see the full list. On macOS, use `⌘` instead of `Ctrl` and `⌥` instead of `Alt`. Shortcuts are not available on the mobile screen.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
heading: Global shortcuts
text:
| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Open a new conversation | `Alt+Shift+N` |
| Move to the composer | `/` (outside a text field) |
| Search conversations and artifacts | `Ctrl+K` |
| Collapse or expand the sidebar | `Ctrl+Shift+S` |
| Copy the last answer | `Alt+Shift+C` |
| Copy the last code block | `Ctrl+Shift+;` |
| Open personalization settings | `Alt+Shift+P` |
| Start or stop dictation | `Ctrl+Shift+M` |
| Delete the conversation | `Ctrl+Shift+⌫` |
| Show the shortcut list | `Ctrl+/` |

title: Keyboard shortcuts
heading: Composer
text:
| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Send | `Enter` |
| New line | `Shift+Enter` |
| Dictate | In an empty composer, hold `Space` while you speak. Release it to type the words into the box (with **Hold Space to dictate** on in Preferences) |

title: Keyboard shortcuts
heading: Document editor and presentation mode
text:
| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Save | `Ctrl+S` |
| Save a source edit | `Ctrl+Enter` |
| Move between slides (presentation mode) | `←` `→` |
| Show presenter notes | `N` |
| Exit presentation mode | `Esc` |

title: Signing up and signing in
text: This page explains how to request an account and sign in, and how to manage your password and your devices.

title: Signing up and signing in
heading: Requesting an account
text:
1. On the sign-in screen, select the **Sign up** tab.
2. Enter your name, email and password, then press **Request sign-up**. The password must be at least 10 characters long and contain a number and a symbol. If the screen lists the addresses that may sign up, only addresses at those domains may apply.
3. What happens next depends on the sign-up method the administrator has set.

| Sign-up method | Right after you apply |
|---|---|
| Use after approval | A waiting screen appears. It checks the status every 15 seconds and moves to the home screen automatically once you are approved. |
| Use immediately | You can start using the service right away, with no waiting. |

If pressing **Request sign-up** shows the notice "Sign-ups are not being accepted at the moment", ask your administrator to create an account for you. Where email verification is configured, a confirmation mail is sent. If it does not arrive, you can send it again after one minute.

title: Signing up and signing in
heading: Signing in
text:
Sign in with your email and password. **If you enter the wrong password five times in a row within 15 minutes, sign-in is blocked for 15 minutes.** While it is blocked, even the correct password will not sign you in. The screen shows the time left, and an administrator's password reset or your own reset lifts it at once.

If your account is suspended, an information screen appears instead of the home screen. In that case, contact your administrator.

title: Signing up and signing in
heading: Resetting your password
text: If the sign-in screen has a **Forgot your password?** link, you can receive a reset mail. The link in the mail is valid for 30 minutes and can be used only once. When you set a new password you are signed in immediately and **every session on your other devices is signed out.** If the link is not shown, no mail server is configured in your environment, so ask your administrator to reset the password for you.

title: Signing up and signing in
heading: Changing your password and managing devices
text:
- Changing your password: Account menu → **Settings** → **Security**. Changing it signs you out on your other devices.
- List of signed-in devices and sign-in history: **Settings** → **Security**. For details, see Settings.

title: Signing up and signing in
heading: Automatic sign-out
text: Where the administrator has set an idle time, you are signed out automatically after that much time with no activity. When you connect again, the sign-in screen shows a notice that you were signed out automatically.

title: Signing up and signing in
heading: Interface language
text: Use the **EN** button at the top right to switch the interface language. The language of an answer follows **the language you asked in**, regardless of the interface language.

title: Artifacts
text: Reports, slides, charts, code, web pages, images and other outputs generated in a conversation are called artifacts. They are collected on the **Artifacts** screen in the sidebar.

title: Artifacts
heading: Artifact panel
text:
- The panel opens automatically when an artifact is generated. If you closed it, reopen it with a button such as **Open the report** or **Open the deck** at the top right of the conversation screen.
- Every panel shows the version and the edit time, and lets you copy, download, adjust the width (double-click to reset), switch between narrow, wide, and document-only views, and close the panel. If the screen is narrow, the panel is shown over the conversation.
- Code and web pages support the **Preview** and **Source** tabs and zooming in and out. A web page runs in an isolated frame, so features that save values do not work.
- In Chat too, a request such as "organize this into a table and turn it into a document" or "draw a chart from this data" generates an artifact in the panel.

title: Artifacts
heading: Export formats
text:
| Type | Formats |
|---|---|
| Report | PDF, Word (DOCX), Hangul (HWPX), the Markdown source, print |
| Slides | PowerPoint (PPTX), PDF, text (with notes) |
| A document with a template applied | PDF, DOCX/PPTX, HWPX, HTML, text |

PDF reproduces the theme as it is, and DOCX and PPTX put an editable structure first, so some visual elements of the template may differ.

title: Artifacts
heading: Gallery
text: See the full list under **Artifacts** in the sidebar. It provides tabs by type (all, code, HTML, report, slides, chart, image, audio, video) and a title search. Selecting a card opens it as a panel inside the gallery. To go to the conversation that generated it, use **Open the original conversation** on the card. Deleting from the gallery deletes the version history as well, but the conversation is kept.

title: Artifact editor
text: You can edit reports and slides directly in the right-hand panel. The features are grouped by the tabs in the ribbon at the top.

title: Artifact editor
heading: Report panel
text:
The ribbon consists of **Home · Edit · Insert · Layout · Review · View · File**.

### Home

Switch between **Web view** and **Page view** (actual A4 pages), and change the document theme (editorial, magazine, minimal), the accent color, and the **Template**. In web view, **Source** lets you edit the whole Markdown.

### Edit

- **Edit document**: edit directly on the page. It supports bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text color, highlighter, line spacing, lists and indentation, quotations, table insertion with row and column operations and merging, page breaks, source citation insertion, find and replace, and undo.
- **Source**: edit the whole Markdown. Save with `Ctrl+Enter`.
- The menu beside a section title adds a section before or after, duplicates, moves up or down, deletes, runs **Rewrite this section only**, and runs a review. The last remaining section cannot be deleted. If you type an instruction into **Rewrite this section only**, only that section is written again.
- Selecting a sentence in the body shows **Fix this passage**. It quotes the selected sentence and asks for a revision.

### Insert

In **Add a picture**, set the section to insert into, how the picture is produced (generate a new one or choose an existing one), and the caption. An inserted picture is part of the file, so it is carried along when you print and share. If the image feature is turned off, you cannot generate a new one.

### Layout

It provides **Page setup** (header, footer, page numbers).

### View

Open and close the **Contents** pane, where you can check progress and the word count. Wide view, document only, and close panel are chosen from the buttons at the top right of the panel, not from the ribbon.

### File

Exports to PDF, Word (DOCX), Hangul (HWPX), the Markdown sourc

title: Artifact editor
heading: Slides panel
text:
The ribbon consists of **Home · Edit · Insert · Review · View · Slide show · File**.

### Home

Choose the slide theme from editorial, minimal, poster, split, dark, steel, warm, pastel, forest, academic, and monochrome, change the accent color, and run **Redo this slide**.

### Edit

- Click text on a slide to edit it directly. You can set bold, italic, size, and color.
- In bulk text box editing, the first line becomes the title and each line becomes an item. A `|` separates the rows of a table.
- It provides speaker notes, table data editing (add, move, and delete rows and columns), and chart editing (bar and line, units, series).
- In the picture tool, upload an image (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, 5MB or less) and set the display mode, the size, and the left or right placement.
- When the content overflows, it supports auto fit, splitting the slide, changing the layout, adjusting the font size, and undo. Save with `Ctrl+S`.
- The slide menu adds a slide before or after, duplicates, moves, deletes, and sets the layout and the font size. You can select several slides to change the accent color and font size in bulk, or to reset the formatting.

### Insert

It provides adding and replacing pictures, and replacing an automatically generated diagram with a picture drawn by an image model.

### View and Slide show

It provides the slide list pane and slide navigation. For presentation mode, see Writing slides.

### File

Exports to PowerPoint (PPTX), PDF, and text (with notes), and supports copying the script.

title: Artifact editor
heading: Review
text:
| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Automatic checks | Checks the document without calling a model. Items that must be fixed (P0: empty content, blocks that were not written, placeholders, unrendered Markdown, Chinese characters mixed into Korean sentences, figures with no evidence, arithmetic errors, the writer's plan or instructions left in place of the text) show as **{n} to fix**. Together with items worth a look (P1: filler phrases, sentences that start with an emoji, repeated lines, too many lines on one slide, lines that run past two rows) they show as **{n} to look at**. Correct them with **Fix it** or **Fix all**. When a section edited from the chat comes back with a P0 it did not have, it is written once more; if the P0 is still there, the section keeps its previous text and the reply says so. For slides it reports **n slides at overflow risk** separately. |
| Ask for a review | The model reads the document once and gives a score out of 10 with up to six points to address. The score is for reference and does not restrict export. |
| Fact check | Compares the claims in a section or a slide against the evidence. A verdict with no source URL is lowered to **Needs checking**. Opinions and definitions are excluded from judgment. |
| Evidence panel (report) | Provides the source list, citation checks, citation styles (APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE), adding material directly, deleting unused material, and the research log (search terms, accepted, excluded). |
| Review notes (slides) | Add notes per slide and mark them resolved or reopened. Unresolved notes are shown with a badge. |
| Version history | See below. |

title: Artifact editor
heading: Version management and conflict handling
text:
A snapshot is saved every time you save, rewrite, or restore. In the ribbon, open **Review → Version history** to see the content of an earlier version, compare the additions, deletions, and edits, and then roll back.

If the same document was edited in another window, it asks you to choose between **Load the latest version** and **Copy my edits**.

title: Artifact editor
heading: Editing limits on documents with a template applied
text: Reports and slides with a template applied support block-level rewriting only, and Markdown source editing is not provided. The export formats are PDF, DOCX/PPTX, HWPX, HTML, and text.

title: Images and audio/video
text: The **Image** and **Audio/Video** tabs appear on the home screen only when the administrator has enabled them. Most of these features use external generation services, so they consume credits, and the estimated credits are shown before you send. Attaching files is not supported.

title: Images and audio/video
heading: Images
text:
Set the image options below the input box.

| Chip | Choices |
|---|---|
| Ratio | 16:9 · 9:16 · 4:3 · 1:1 (only the ones the model supports) |
| Style | **Picture**: Auto · photo · illustration · infographic · watercolor**Exact figure**: structure diagram · flow diagram · concept diagram · chartPrompt as written |
| Text | Auto · Korean · English · none |

One picture is made at a time. The **Picture** group is drawn by the picture model; the **Exact figure** group is drawn as shapes or a chart without it, so its text is exact. **Prompt as written** sends the text to the picture model unchanged.

Pick the picture model from the model name at the right of the composer. The list comes from the models registered in the model gateway; the default setup's external picture models are Seedream 5.0 Flash, Recraft V4.1, Grok Imagine Image 2.0, GPT-5.4 Image 2 and Gemini 3 Pro Image. When the administrator connects a self-hosted picture model, strict-local picture models appear as well. Pictures in a project conversation, a conversation with attachments, or a strict-local conversation are drawn by strict-local models only. Privacy

The result card provides enlarged view, download, **Generate again**, **Fix the prompt**, and **View the prompt sent** (the final sentence that was actually sent). A chart is drawn as code by the text model. You can use **View the drawing code** and **Redraw with this code**. If you choose a model that does not support ratio settings, a message tells you that the image is generated as a square.

**Structure, flow and concept diagrams** do not use the image model. The text model writes the description as a flowchart, and the server draws it with the same shapes as the diagrams in reports and slides and keeps it as a picture. If there are too many steps

title: Images and audio/video
heading: Audio
text: Generates narration (with a voice choice) or music at 15, 30, 60, or 120 seconds. The result comes with a player and a download, and narration also shows the script. Audio is charged per generation.

title: Images and audio/video
heading: Video
text: Set the ratio, the resolution (720p or 1080p), whether there is sound, and the length (4 to 10 seconds). Video generation takes a long time, so the card shows the progress. You can still see the finished result after refreshing the screen or connecting from another device. You can cancel a generation. Credits are deducted only when it completes. If you choose a combination that the model does not price, a message saying "This model does not produce this combination" appears and sending is blocked. The theme does not apply to audio and video.

title: Writing reports
text: On the home screen, select **Report** and enter the topic of the report you want to write. If you have supporting material, attach it from **+** → **Attach files or photos** in the composer. When you attach material, KloudChat fills the figures in from that material instead of estimating them. Where a search server is connected, it searches the web before writing and cites the sources. A request about domestic research trends or one that names KCI also finds KCI, DBpia and RISS papers through the same search and cites their authors, year, journal and DOI.

title: Writing reports
heading: Step 1: Confirming the structure
text:
KloudChat does not write the document right away. It proposes a **structure** first. If it lacks information it needs for writing, a **Before we start** card appears ahead of the structure and asks clarifying questions. Answer them, or select **Proceed with the material available**, and it moves on to the structure step.

- You can edit section titles, change their order, and add or delete sections. After editing, **Back to the proposal** restores the original.
- The structure card covers content only. Choose the document theme after writing, from **Edit → Theme** in the ribbon.
- Press **Generate as it is**, or **Generate with my changes** if you edited anything, and writing begins.
- If you type a sentence into the input box below the card, it proposes the structure again with that sentence as a condition. You can only approve it with the buttons.
- If the topic needs diagrams or pictures, an **Add pictures?** card follows. It tells you the number of pictures and the estimated credits. Diagrams (flowcharts and structure charts) are written as a flow by the text model and drawn as shapes by the server, so they do not consume image credits. Pictures are drawn by the image model.

title: Writing reports
heading: Step 2: Writing
text:
It writes section by section in order, and shows the first section in the right-hand panel as soon as it is complete. A section that fails is marked as failed, and writing continues for the remaining sections.

The default look is an official document: body text justified, a navy accent, and plain statements with their basis instead of strong adjectives. Numbers stay in the sentences and tables that use them; there is no separate strip of key figures at the end. Change the colour and theme from **Edit → Theme** on the ribbon.

title: Writing reports
heading: Step 3: Revising
text:
Two methods are provided.

- **Revise by request**: type into the input box at the bottom of the document, for example "Cut section 2 in half" or "Add one more section". Revising by request
- **Edit directly**: use the ribbon in the panel to edit sentences, reorder sections, insert pictures, and get a review. Artifact editor

title: Writing reports
heading: Items you can specify in your request
text:
| Example input | What it does |
|---|---|
| "In four sections" | Sets the number of sections. The range is 3 to 12. |
| "Review report", "weekly report", "meeting minutes", "incident report" | Applies a structure that suits the document type. Only documents that call for a judgment include summary and recommendation sections. |
| Selecting a template from **+** → Pick a template | Applies the structure rules and typesetting of that template. |

title: Writing reports
heading: Export
text: In the ribbon, open **File → Export** and choose PDF, Word (DOCX), Hangul (HWPX), the Markdown source, or print. If any item has evidence that is not confirmed, it tells you before exporting. PDF reproduces the theme as it is, and DOCX puts an easily editable structure first.

title: Revising by request
text:
Type what you want changed into the input box at the bottom of a finished report or slide deck. It analyzes the request and decides for itself which part to change and how. For sentence-level edits or reordering slides, the Artifact editor is faster.

| Example request | How it is handled |
|---|---|
| "Cut section 2 in half", "add a schedule table to the conclusion" | Writes only that part again. The rest is kept. |
| "Drop the table in section 2 and put a 3-line summary at the top" | Writes again only the parts each ask points at. The summary goes at the top of the first section as a 「핵심」 box with exactly the lines asked, without repeating the title or author line. |
| "Remove table 2 and figure 1" | Takes out the numbered tables and figures as they are, without rewriting. Sentences that pointed at them are tidied, and the numbers of later tables and figures, and the references to them, close up. Rewriting that section in the same request puts no new table or figure in their place. A number that is not in the document is reported as not found. |
| "Make the whole thing more concise", "change the tone to polite form" | Writes every part again. |
| "Extend it to 20 slides", "add 3 slides", "merge 2 and 3", "change the order" | Proposes the structure again, waits for your approval, and then writes. Parts that are kept reuse their existing titles. |
| A question about the document, such as "how many slides are there?" | Not answered on this screen and nothing is changed. The reply asks you to name what to change, and to ask about the content in Chat with the downloaded file attached. |
| "Write it again", "start over", "with a different topic" | Keeps the existing document and writes a new one. |

When the revision is finished, the message says what was done for each ask

title: Sharing
text: Create a link with the **Share** button at the top right of the conversation screen.

title: Sharing
heading: Creating a link
text:
1. Choose who can see it.

   | Scope | Who can view it |
   |---|---|
   | People with an account | Every user signed in to this service. Restrictions by department or team do not apply. |
   | People with the link | Anyone who knows the link. No account is needed. |

2. Press **Create the link** and then **Copy**.

After creation, the status is shown as **Account required** or **Opens without an account**.

title: Sharing
heading: What is shared
text:
- The conversation and the artifacts generated in it are made public. The artifact is shown first, and the conversation follows. For some types, a message says that the share screen does not support them yet.
- **Project files and memory are not shared.** Files attached to the conversation are exposed only to the extent that the answer quotes them.
- **Conversation that continues after sharing keeps appearing in the link as well.** To make only part of it public up to a certain point, revoke the link and create a new one.

title: Sharing
heading: View history and revocation
text: In the same window you can check the viewer (name and email, or "visitor without an account"), the browser, the region, and the number of views. Repeat views within one hour are counted as one. When you run **Revoke the link**, the link stops working immediately. The link is also blocked if you delete the conversation.

title: Writing slides
text: On the home screen, select **Slides** and enter the presentation topic and the audience. The procedure is the same as for a report. It runs through clarifying questions, the **structure check**, the **Add pictures?** card, and then writing slide by slide.

title: Writing slides
heading: Items in the structure check
text:
- Slide titles and their order
- **How will this be used?**: presenting with narration, or handing over the material only

The theme is not chosen on the structure card. After writing, choose it in the panel from editorial, minimal, poster, split, dark, steel, warm, pastel, forest, academic, and monochrome.

title: Writing slides
heading: Setting the number of slides
text:
| Example input | What it does |
|---|---|
| "6 slides", "a 20-slide deck" | Writes the number of slides you set. The maximum is 50. |
| "a 20-minute presentation" | Calculates the minimum number of slides at one slide per two minutes. 20 minutes gives at least 10 slides. |
| Not specified | Writes 5 to 12 slides to suit the topic. |

If the deck runs to more than 6 slides, a table of contents is inserted as the second slide.

title: Writing slides
heading: Slide types
text: The model chooses the type that suits the content. It uses cover, table of contents, item list, table (comparison), metrics (key figures), chart (when the material contains figures), diagram (flow and structure), and closing. You can set them in your request, for example "use a table for the comparison" or "include a flow chart". The server draws diagrams as shapes, and a PPTX export carries them as editable PowerPoint shapes. A slide whose title names a structure, a relationship or a flow ("Overall structure", "Object relationships", "Request flow") gets a diagram even when the request never says "diagram", and a relationship is drawn as lines named with each relation rather than as a chain of arrows. After the deck is made, "turn slide 4 into a structure diagram" redraws that slide as one. A deck written in English gets English diagram labels and captions.

title: Writing slides
heading: Changing the theme
text: In the panel's **Edit › Theme** tab you can change the theme and the accent color, and run **Redo this slide**. If a theme is linked to the project, the deck follows its colors and typefaces.

title: Writing slides
heading: Presentation mode
text: Switch to full screen from **Slide show** in the ribbon. Move between slides with `←` and `→`, and exit with `Esc`. It provides a presentation timer, speaker notes shown with the `N` key, and a slide list.

title: Writing slides
heading: Export
text: In **File → Export**, choose PowerPoint (PPTX), PDF (for presenting), or text (with notes). If there are slides at overflow risk, slides whose evidence needs checking, or unresolved review notes, it tells you before exporting. **Copy the script** copies the slide body text and the speaker notes at once. The dark impression applies to PPTX only, and PDF is output on a light background.

title: Writing slides
heading: Revising
text: If you ask for something like "make slide 2 more concise", only that slide is written again. A request that changes the structure, such as "extend it to 20 slides" or "add a case study slide", proposes the structure again and waits for your approval. For details, see Revising by request. To edit sentences yourself or reorder slides, use the Artifact editor.
